(b) **A `var` redeclaring a PARAMETER shares the parameter's slot.** The graph's lexical resolution unions the FUNCTION-scope frame's hits with every same-name hoisting-kind binding wherever written (inner block-scoped frames stay exact, so shadowing is preserved), the content lowering resolves a hoisted-`var` name as `SliceExpr::Local` / `CallOnBinding` AHEAD of the parameter list, and both carry the parameter ordinal so an unbound read (before the declarator, or on a path that never reached it) still resolves to the parameter — never a fabricated `any`. (c) **Loop transparency requires transfer-inert selected content.** A return-free loop stays `TransparentLoop` only when it declares no escaping `var` and its body has no live selected-slot guard, call/assertion, or write whose iteration flow can change a downstream selected read. Read/write comparison is path-aware: statically distinct member siblings do not alias, while whole-root and computed segments remain conservative. Literal-dead `if` branches and a `while (false)` body contribute neither loop transfer nor unapplied-write degradation. Nested closure effects are inspected only for a function/arrow in CALLEE position — callback arguments are values, not proven invocations — and a directly invoked closure inside a loop fails closed when its own skeleton writes a captured downstream slot or reads one in a control/call site. Such iteration-dependent flow requires a fixed point the substrate does not model, so it takes the typed `SliceUnsupported::Loop` no-value rail and cannot warm. A control read with no modelled guard (`while (x + 1)`), a callback argument, and a loop with no selected capture remain transparent; precise closure-guard transfer remains deferred.
- **A bare direct invocation cannot publish an unmodeled closure transfer.** An expression statement whose callee is an inline function/arrow is checked against the downstream selected slot. If that closure writes the capture or reads it in a guard/control position, the slice takes the typed `InvokedClosureEffect` no-value rail with zero candidates. This is intentionally conservative: the substrate does not yet apply the single-invocation closure's narrowing overlay, so discarding the effect and warming the pre-invocation union would be unsound.
- **Declarator annotations SUPPLY a stable assignment and mutable-capture authority.** A declarator's authored TS annotation lowers onto `SliceStatement::Binding.declared` through the same shallow pass a `SliceExpr::Type` leaf carries. Lexical declarations seed that authority at their source-ordered binding statement; selected `var` annotations seed it at frame entry because both assignment checking and a forward read observe the hoisted declared type before the initializer (`X66_hoisted_annotated_var_authority_serves_forward_read`). Runtime values remain source-ordered: an initializer executes at its statement, and an initializer-less `var` performs NO runtime write, so `x = "b"; var x: "a" | "b"; return x` keeps the assignment-reduced `"b"`. With no preceding reaching value, an initializer-less annotated declaration still supplies its declared type (`var y: number | undefined;` is `number | undefined`, not the unbound implicit `any`). A destructured parameter element seeds both its reaching value and declared authority before its first read OR write, so a preceding write is reduced against the annotated member union. A non-union annotated initializer publishes the declared type (`const y: string = "s"` is `string`; `const y: "s" = "s"` still pins `"s"`); a declared union is assignment-reduced to comparable DECLARED constituents for both its initializer and later whole-binding writes (`let x: "a" | "b" = "a"; x = "b"` reaches `"b"`). A nested function value carries the exact declared authority for each captured mutable `let`/`var` and parameter element, keyed by binding identity rather than reconstructed from a current value. A reaching `let` value remains the closure's read authority until that closure writes it; `var` and forward-`let` captures retain authored authority. The declared node rides a separate lexical/function-scoped map from the changing reaching value, including scope-shadow close and layer snapshots, so a later write never reconstructs authorship from the current value. Assignment-context object literals retain a pre-property-widening member view solely for constituent selection. When mutually assignable object arms differ by exact present keys or discriminants, that evidence can select the best-matching declared arm; spread programs deliberately bypass exact-key selection because their final key set is not closed. Generic strict-subtype dominance is not a checker rule here: required-property presence alone does not discard an overlapping optional-property constituent. Ordinary object evaluation still uses mutable-property widening. `X65_object_assignment_declared_union_selects_matching_arm`, `X69_overlapping_object_union_assignment_selects_narrow_arm`, `X75_fresh_object_assignment_selects_optional_member_arm`, `X76_fresh_computed_object_assignment_selects_optional_member_arm`, `X77_spread_object_assignment_preserves_declared_union`, and `X84_required_property_assignment_preserves_optional_union_arm` pin those boundaries.
- **Abrupt-edge state is point-in-time and scope-closed.** Break, return, and throw edges each capture the complete reaching-definition state where the edge occurs. Every crossed lexical scope replays its shadow close onto those snapshots before a construct joins them; `if` arms likewise snapshot only after closing the arm scope. A `finally` entry joins normal completions, throw points, and pending break/return pre-states. Return inference aggregates every authored try/catch/finally return even when an abrupt `finally` overrides runtime completion, while the pending control edges exposed to an enclosing construct still obey that override: an abrupt finally replaces pre-finally returns and breaks but preserves returns and breaks authored by the finally itself. A pending named break overridden by an abrupt finally remains an implicit-`undefined` return-inference contributor when its target statement has no following current-function return; that holds for both a directly labelled try (`X68_finally_return_over_labelled_break_keeps_undefined`) and a try wrapped by labelled blocks (`X80_wrapped_labelled_try_finally_keeps_undefined`). A following return suppresses that contributor, preserving `X52_finally_entry_joins_pending_break`. Switch dispatch death is independent of a live clause fall-through chain: exhausting the no-match edge cannot delete fall-through into `default`.
- **Logical guard facts are edge-asymmetric when an operand is unmodelled.** The guard tree preserves `SliceGuard::None` operands instead of simplifying them away. On `modelled && opaque()`, the true edge may apply the modelled fact but the false edge cannot negate it; on `modelled || opaque()`, the true edge establishes nothing while the false edge may negate every modelled disjunct. Predicate leaves retain their negation bit, so De Morgan transformation is reversible: the surviving edge of `!(isStr(x) && opaque)` recovers the original positive predicate rather than erasing it. A disjunction evaluates every alternative from the same starting overlay and joins each alternative's FINAL value per subject; intermediate conjunction facts never become separate union contributors (`N21_guard_union_uses_final_alternative_overlay`, `N22_double_negated_guard_union_uses_final_alternative_overlay`). An alternative whose sequential conjunction has no surviving declared arm is represented as impossible and contributes no overlay to the disjunction (`N23_impossible_conjunction_drops_dead_disjunction_alternative`). This is one `And`/`Or` authority consumed in positive and negative modes, not two pattern-specific rewrites.
- **Guaranteed-return qualifier for labelled-break inference.** In the preceding abrupt-edge rule, a “following current-function return” means a suffix statement that guarantees the return on every normal path (a direct return, a sequential block containing one, or both arms of an `if`). The qualifier is inherited through recursively lowered blocks and labels: an abrupt `finally` retains a pending named break as a return-inference-only suffix edge when the crossed target carries it. A suffix contributor already strictly covered by an ordinary return is redundant; an incomparable suffix remains in the inferred union. Merely containing a conditional return does not suppress the implicit-`undefined` contributor.
- **The root-identifier gate.** The shared shallow-pass leaf lowering (`infer_declaration_expression_type`) has NO frame — it resolves every name it meets in FILE OWNER SCOPE. So every leaf answer the slice content mints routes through ONE gate (`flow_slice_content.rs` — `Lowerer::leaf_type`, the sole producer of a leaf answer). Two evidence sources, one verdict: (a) the ANSWER's names, read off the produced typed IR through the shared exhaustive walk `verter_type_expr::referenced_names` (`typeof x…` value-path roots + named type references — never a re-derivation of the leaf's own traversal), and (b) for an answer the leaf could not model at all (a bare `any`), the expression's REFERENCE-CHAIN root (`a`, `a.b`, `a["b"]`, `a.#b`, `a?.b`, `a.b()`, `new a()`, `` a`…` ``, through parentheses and TS wrappers). A frame-owned name in (b) fails closed immediately (`SliceExpr::UnmodeledBinding` — no answer exists and no owner scope could supply one; POSITIONALLY, as the typed unresolved marker). A frame-owned name in (a) rides the `SliceExpr::FrameShadowed { inner, shadowed }` carrier, and the EVALUATOR decides against the live owner scope (`flow_return.rs` — the one shared `owner_scope_answers_frame_name` probe, taken through the same lowering the answer itself would take: `typeof name` for a value reference, a bare `name` reference for a type or namespace one; the head of `N.B` is the same scope lookup as a bare `N`, so the meanings differ on the FRAME side, not here): a name the owner scope ANSWERS fails closed positionally (the marker + `UnmodeledPosition`), a name it answers nothing for evaluates the wrapped leaf unchanged, because nothing can be mis-bound and the leaf's own typed miss is the honest result. Without the gate, `class CBait { static s = 1 } return CBait.s` published the module-scope `CBait`'s type, and `{ ...param }` / `param.m()` / `[localConst]` / `c ? localConst : 2` published the module-scope homonym's — cleanly and WARM. The `any`-half deliberately does NOT scan the whole subtree: a name in a position the leaf never consumes (a conditional TEST in `c ? 1 : 2`, an assignment target in `{ a: (x = "s") }`, a call argument) says nothing about the answer.
- **The frame gate covers every `TypeExpr` ENTRANCE, not just leaves — structurally.** Slice content mints types at eight `TypeExpr`-bearing fields, and each one is a place the frame-less shallow pass can hand back an owner-scope answer for a frame-owned name. Six of them (`SliceParam.ty` from an annotation, from a rest annotation, and from a default-initializer inference; `SliceTypeParam.constraint` / `.default`; `SliceStatement::Binding.declared`) hold the `GatedType` newtype (`flow_slice_content.rs`), whose `ty` / `shadowed` fields are PRIVATE and whose only two constructors are `Lowerer::gate` and the explicitly-named `GatedType::root_signature` — so "mint a slice-content type without deciding what the frame does to it" does not compile. The remaining two (`SliceExpr::Type` / `SliceCall::Symbolic`) ride the `SliceExpr::FrameShadowed` carrier from `Lowerer::leaf_type`, which additionally needs the `FrameShadowedRoot` `any`-arm annotations do not. The two free producers `lower_params` / `lower_slice_type_params` take a NON-defaultable `SignatureScope::{Root, Nested}`, so a new call site must choose the scope. `SliceStatement::Binding.declared` must be gated on the ANNOTATION itself: with a non-union declared type the evaluator binds the declared node and never evaluates the initializer, so the initializer's own gate cannot stand in.
- **Root signature vs nested signature (`resolveName`, `lastLocation !== location.body`).** A function's body-local type declarations are in scope ONLY inside its own body — never in its own parameter list, type-parameter clause, or parameter defaults (TypeScript discards a Type-meaning hit in a function-like `location`'s `locals` when `lastLocation !== location.body`; the value side mirrors it in `useOuterVariableScopeInParameter`). So the ROOT function's signature stays UNGATED (`SignatureScope::Root` ⇒ `GatedType::root_signature`) while a NESTED function value's signature — which sits inside the enclosing body — is gated against the ENCLOSING frame at the nested value's own span (`SignatureScope::Nested`). Gating the root positions would fail closed on `function f(p: Info) { class Info {} … }`, where the OUTER `Info` is correct. A parameter DEFAULT initializer additionally carries its reference-chain root as a `FrameShadowedName::Value`: a widened or primitive answer (`p = C` ⇒ `string`) names nothing at all while still having read THROUGH a frame binding.
- **A nested signature's OWN type parameters are BINDERS, in TYPE meaning only.** They are the names the evaluator's nested `flow_binder_env` interns, so an answer naming one resolves to the binder and a captured same-named `class` / `enum` does not shadow it (`Lowerer::name_is_frame_bound` subtracts them). In NAMESPACE meaning the binder still wins lexically but denotes no namespace, so a qualified `T.B` is unresolvable and stays frame-bound (fail-closed). The SHARED walk `verter_type_expr::referenced_names` masks the same class structurally: a `Function` / `ConstructorType` / method / call-signature node opens a binder frame over its own subtree on the same explicit heap work-stack the rest of the walk uses (depth-safe, exhaustive), so a generic function type in an ANSWER never reports its own `<T>` as a scope reference.
- **Type-space lookups are MEANING-filtered, and the meaning is per OCCURRENCE.** A bare `N` reference demands a `Type` meaning; the HEAD of a qualified `N.B` demands a `Namespace` meaning (`SymbolFlags.Namespace = ValueModule | NamespaceModule | Enum` — a class is NOT in it). `FunctionBodySkeleton::declares_meaning_in_scope(name, region, NameMeaning)` walks the region chain filtering by `SkeletonBindingKind::declares(meaning)` at EVERY hop (a scope whose symbol lacks the meaning is skipped and the walk continues outward), and `bindings_of_name_in_scope` is symmetric — it filters by `SkeletonBindingKind::declares_value()` at every hop, so the TYPE-ONLY kinds are transparent to a value lookup. Oracle-anchored cells (`tsc --strict`, one fixture per cell): `class` (± statics) and `type` / `interface` shadow the bare reference but NOT the qualified head; `namespace` is the reverse; `enum` / `const enum` shadow both; every value-only kind (`const` / `let` / `var` / `function` / parameter / catch-param) shadows neither; `class N` + `namespace N` shadows both while `function N` + `namespace N` shadows only the head. `import N = …` is meaning-TRANSPARENT (it occupies exactly its target's spaces), which the skeleton cannot decide, so it answers BOTH conservatively — a recorded over-fire that can only fail closed. The `qualified` bit rides `verter_type_expr::ReferencedTypeName` PER OCCURRENCE, because one answer can reference the same head both ways. `CaptureScope` therefore carries `type_names` and `namespace_names` as two SEPARATE inventories, and `FrameShadowedName` splits `Type` / `Namespace` alongside `Value`.
- **A named function expression's own name is a binding of its OWN frame.** `FunctionBodySource::from_function_expression` carries the expression's `id` into the nested `FunctionBodySkeleton` as a `SkeletonBindingKind::NestedFunction` binding of the ROOT region, so `const g = function h() { … h … }` resolves `h` through the nested frame's lexical authority (fail-closed, like every nested function declaration) instead of looking FREE and escaping to an enclosing or module-scope `h`. A function DECLARATION keeps `from_function` — its name binds in the ENCLOSING scope. Consequently `SliceCall::DirectSelf` is minted only where the frame owns a flow slot: `FlowEvaluator::self_slot` is `Option<&FlowReturnKey>` and is `None` inside every nested function value, so an inner self-call can no longer take a hold on the ENCLOSING function's slot.
- **A block-level function declaration is BLOCK-scoped.** `FunctionBodySkeleton::hoisting_bindings_of_name` hoists `SkeletonBindingKind::Var` unconditionally but a `NestedFunction` only when its recorded region is the frame's ROOT region: in strict-mode ESM (every carrier surface this substrate serves) a block-level function declaration is block-scoped, and only Annex-B sloppy-mode semantics create the function-scoped alias. Hoisting it unconditionally made `if (c) { function f() {…} } return f()` resolve to the block's function and FAIL CLOSED where the correct answer is the module-scope `f`'s return. (Latent, no live consumer: `StatementListInventory.nested_function_names` in `function_program.rs` carries no region axis.)
- **The interim `DirectCall` annotation rail (final semantics: U6.CALL_RESOLVE).** A value declaration carrying BOTH an authored annotation and an initializer is typed by the ANNOTATION — the initializer only has to be assignable to it. The direct-call rail therefore checks the target's prepared value decl for an authored annotation (`ValueAnnotationClass::Direct` / `TypeOfAlias` with a `SemanticTypeSource::Authored` source) and, when present, resolves the callee as a VALUE TYPE through the same shared path a parenthesised or ambient callee takes (`call_return_of_callee_node`), never through the initializer's own flow position: `const f: () => 42 = () => 42; f()` is `42`, not the initializer arrow's inferred `number`. FINAL declarator-annotated call semantics are owned by `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`; this rail is the interim HONEST answer, not the finished mechanism.
- **A CALLEE's own clause instantiates AT THE CALL SITE, on every route (sb15).** Whatever a callee answers with — its body-derived flow return, its DECLARED return carrier, or a resolved signature node's return position — is expressed in the CALLEE's own type-parameter binders, so handing it back verbatim publishes the callee's generic parameter as the caller's whole-function return, cleanly and warm. That is unsound rather than merely imprecise, because the evaluator's binder identity is file-scoped and name-keyed (`DeclIdentity::from_scope(file_scope, name)`, `param_index: 0`): an enclosing `class Holder<T>` and a same-named callee parameter intern to ONE `SemanticNodeId`, so the leaked binder is substitutable by an instantiation that has nothing to do with it (`new Holder<number>().viaCall()` answering `number`).

  **The rule is structurally confined, not per-arm.** Every call form rides ONE `SliceExpr::Call(SliceCall, SliceCallSite)` carrier over a closed six-variant vocabulary (`Nested` / `OnBinding` / `LocalFunctionShadow` / `DirectSelf` / `Direct` / `Symbolic`, `flow_slice_content.rs`), and the evaluator answers them in ONE exhaustive `FlowEvaluator::eval_call` whose sink type is `CallValue` (`project_semantic_dispatch::flow_return_callee`). **That closes the call VOCABULARY; whether a call REACHES it is the content lowering's separate obligation, and it is held by two more rails.** Expression-form exhaustiveness lives in the SHARED classifier `analysis::flow::value_descent`, not in `Lowerer::lower_expr`: `lower_expr` handles the frame-local carriers (identifier, nested function value, call) and ends in `other => match value_descent(other)`, and it is the classifier's wildcard-free match over `Expression` that refuses to compile for a new variant — which is what makes the disposition binding on the demand PLANNER as well (see the `FunctionBodySkeleton` bullet). A wildcard is what let a CONDITIONAL expression sit silently in the leaf list, folding `return c ? f() : g()` through the frame-less shallow pass into an unreduced `ReturnType<callee>` carrier that was published warm with the callee's own binders intact and its overload group unconsulted, while the `if` / `return` twin of the same body went through `SliceCall` and degraded correctly. A conditional is now a `ValueDescent::Branches` disposition (`SliceExpr::Union` over both branch values, joined through the same normalizing interner the contributor join uses), and a leaf answer that EMBEDS the shallow pass's own call-return carrier (`type_eval_build::embeds_call_return_carrier`, read through the shared exhaustive `referenced_names` walk, the predicate colocated with the ONE site that mints the carrier) is `SliceExpr::UnreducedCallValue` and takes the POSITIONAL disposition — the typed unresolved marker contributed AT the position with `FlowReturnDegradation::UnmodeledPosition` recorded — never a published carrier holding a foreign binder, and never a discarded composite. **That carrier gate alone was narrower than the promise it delivered, and the gap is now closed at the FORM rather than at the answer.** The shallow pass's per-expression lowering ends in `_ => Ok(Primitive(Any))` and `lower_leaf`'s `is_any` arm runs BEFORE the carrier gate, so a form whose leaf answer is a bare `any` never reached the gate at all — `new f()`, `` tag`…` ``, `f?.()`, `await f()`, `(k, f())`, `f()!`, `this.m()`, `super.m()` and an unrepresentable computed callee (`obj[sym]()`) all published a fabricated `any` cleanly and warm under a promise that a call with no structural arm fails closed. The call-position verdict is now the classifier's `ValueDescent::UnmodeledCall` (predicate `analysis::flow::value_is_unmodeled_call`, the single authority both `value_descent` and `lower_leaf`'s residual type-carrier check delegate to), plus the `CallExpression` arm's own unrepresentable-callee case, so every one of those fails closed POSITIONALLY whatever the shallow pass answered. **The line is FABRICATION, not the form's own value.** The earlier line — "the form's OWN value IS a call's return" — left every JOIN (`k || f()`, `k ?? f()`), PROJECTION (`f().q`, `f()["q"]`, `f?.()?.q`), OPERATOR (`f() + "x"`), ASSIGNMENT (`z = f()`) and ARRAY-ELEMENT (`["s", new Box()]`) form publishing the shallow pass's fabricated `any`, clean and warm. It was justified as "`any` is UNDER the checker's answer, never over it". That justification is UNSOUND: `any` is BIDIRECTIONALLY assignable, so it is neither under nor over — it silences every check in both directions and is indistinguishable from an authored `any` at every downstream gate. Being under the checker was never the property that made a value publishable; being DISTINGUISHABLE from a known one is. The gate is now `leaf_answer_is_fabricated_at_a_call_position` (`flow_slice_content.rs`): the answer embeds the call-return carrier, OR the answer embeds `any` AND `analysis::flow::value_composes_unmodeled_call` says the expression's value composes over a call with no structural arm. The conjunction is what prevents over-refusal — a form whose answer the pass DOES model (`f() === 1` is `boolean`, `f() as T` is `T`) embeds no `any` and passes, and an AUTHORED `any` (`x as any`) composes no call and passes. `AssignmentExpression` is in `value_is_unmodeled_call` for the same reason `SequenceExpression` is: an assignment's value IS its right-hand side. A JSX attribute's call is likewise NOT routed here: a JSX element's value is `JSX.Element` and does not depend on any attribute's value, so the element's `any` is the shallow pass's fallback row, not a call position. Acceptance: `an_unmodeled_call_position_fails_closed_whatever_the_shallow_pass_answered` + `non_call_forms_and_modeled_call_arms_are_untouched_by_the_call_position_gate` + `flow_return_leaf_answered_call_forms_publish_any_not_a_carrier` (the recorded boundary table). Closing the shallow pass's `_ => Any` disposition is `U6.VALUE_INFERENCE` debt (row FR-D4 below), not this rail's. `CallValue`'s field is PRIVATE and every constructor lives in that module, so "hand a callee's return back untouched" does not compile at a call site — the no-op is reachable only by naming a NON-GENERIC `CalleeClause` (`CalleeClause::non_generic`), a statement about the callee rather than an omission. `CalleeClause` is deliberately NOT `Default`, and a route that cannot READ the clause cannot mint one — STRUCTURALLY: `CalleeClause::non_generic` / `::new` and `CalleeClauseParam::bare` / `::with_default` are all PRIVATE to `flow_return_callee.rs`, so the three fabrications a reviewer planted (`non_generic()` on a serve miss, `new(iter::empty())` on an index miss, `new([bare("Invented")])` from nothing) now fail to compile with `E0624` instead of building clean. The two clause entrances each demand the callee's own AUTHORITY as an argument: `CalleeClause::read_from_program_entry` (the call-site rule) and `read_from_program_entry_at_unknown` (the signature-UTILITY policy) take a `FunctionProgramMatch` — a private-field witness minted ONLY by a keyed lookup on a `FunctionProgramIndex` (`get` / `value_function` / `matches_named`); `CallValue::of_signature_node` reads the clause off a resolved `Signature` node. A bare `&FunctionProgramEntry` was NOT that witness, though the module doc claimed the reference itself was proof of a successful lookup. Two defeats compiled against it, and closing only the obvious one would have left the dangerous one: a struct literal assembled out of nothing (now blocked because `FunctionProgramEntry` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so no other crate can construct one by literal OR by `Clone` + functional update), and — the realistic one — an index MISS falling back to `index.entries.first()`, handing the reader a genuine entry for the WRONG callee and reading that callee's clause as this one's. `FunctionProgramIndex::entries` is private with no positional accessor, so every way out of the index NAMES the position it wants; the two plants now fail with `E0639` / `E0308` and `E0616` respectively. What remains a convention, deliberately, is that the caller looks up the callee it meant: a witness for a deliberately-wrong KEY is still a witness, and binding the key to the callee's identity end-to-end is `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`'s. A serve or index miss has nothing to hand over and returns `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable` (or `None`), which routes to the `UnrepresentableCallee` degradation. The two routes are now SYMMETRIC on a miss: `instantiate_callee_clause_at_unknown` used to return the callee's body-derived return UNTOUCHED — its own binders published warm — where the call-site route degraded on the identical miss. Collapsing that into "the callee is not generic" is how a lookup FAILURE hands the callee's return back verbatim, binders and all, with no degradation and full warm admission. The SCC fixed point is confined the same way: a hold carries its callee's clause (`HeldCallee`), and `HeldCallee::discharged` is the only accessor turning a hold target's admitted result into a join arm, so the equation cannot re-run the transfer around the gate. Exactly one exemption exists and is named: `HeldCallee::own_frame`, the direct SELF-call, whose callee IS the calling frame — its binders are the frame's own and must survive (`f<T>(x: T): T` stays `T`, not `T | unknown`).

  The route inventory, all gated: (1) a resolved callee VALUE TYPE (`call_return_of_callee_node`, reached from the annotated-declarator direct call and from the symbolic `ReturnType<typeof …>` carrier); (2) an IIFE's inline nested signature; (3) a call on a function-typed local / parameter / captured BINDING; (4) a direct call's body-derived FLOW return; (5) a direct call's DECLARED return carrier; (6) the SCC fixed-point discharge. Routes (1)–(3) read the clause off the signature node itself (`CallValue::of_signature_node`); routes (4)–(6) take it as a `CalleeClause` because the flow rail's callee answers with a bare return node and never composes a signature.

  A SEVENTH consumer takes a value from a callee's return position without being a CALL at all: `flow_return_member_projection` (`walk.rs` → `flow_return.rs`), the path-precise `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` rail. It is the signature-UTILITY policy, not the call policy — `ReturnType<…>` has no call site to be argument-free at, so every free clause parameter instantiates at `unknown` and a declared default never applies (`ReturnType<typeof f>` and `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` over `f<MG = number>(x: MG)` are both `unknown`-valued, checker-verified). It applies that policy through `instantiate_named_params_at_unknown` over clause NAMES read from the shallow `FunctionProgramIndex`, NOT by composing the callee's signature: a whole-signature composition here would materialise exactly the sibling members the member demand exists to leave cold. Returning the demand's return position RAW published the callee's own binder as the consumer's value, and made the whole-return route and its one-segment-longer sibling disagree about one callee.

  Four details make it hold. (a) The flow rail's clause is read from the per-file `FunctionProgramIndex` entry's `type_parameters`, keyed by the target's exact program identity, NOT from the prepared value declaration — the value registry does not carry a namespace-scoped function at all, and reading the clause there leaves exactly those callees leaking. (b) The name-driven binder collection can claim THREE resolution states of one clause parameter — the bound `TypeParam`, the deferred `BareRef`, and the RESOLVED `DeclRef` — and WHICH of them it claims is chosen per route by `ClauseSpelling`, because the answer depends on PROVENANCE and the name alone cannot supply it. A declaration's own parameter is not in scope where its DECLARED return locator lowers (file owner scope), so `f<T>(): T` interns its return as an unbound `BareRef("T")`, and when the file ALSO declares a type named `T` that owner-scope lowering RESOLVES the head to the wrong symbol (`interface Item {}` beside `function first<Item>(xs: Item[]): Item`) — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithOwnerScopeResolution`, used by routes whose node came from an owner-scope-lowered declared return (the direct call's DECLARED carrier, and the resolved callee VALUE TYPE). A BODY-DERIVED return is the opposite case: it is evaluated in the callee's own frame where the clause IS bound, so its parameters are already `TypeParam` binders and a resolved `DeclRef` reached through such an arm is by construction a DIFFERENT symbol — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithDeferredHeads`, used by the flow rail, the SCC discharge, an IIFE's composed signature, and the function-typed BINDING route (`SliceCall::OnBinding`). The binding route is the one that has to be argued rather than read off the carrier: a binding's value is either a composed signature (built in the callee's own frame) or a `<T>(x: T) => T` annotation (lowered with its clause in scope), so BOTH spell the clause as binders, and the one shape that could carry an owner-scope misresolution — `typeof declaredFn` — never reaches a `Signature` node on that route at all (it resolves to a non-callable surface and takes the `NonCallableBinding` degradation). ## Tagged-Component Publication: Root Admission Commits, Members Backfill

A mixed `Relate` / `FlowReturn` / `ResolveCall` component closes as ONE decision, but it does NOT publish as one indivisible write. The contract is two-tiered:

- **Root admission is the COMMIT BOUNDARY.** The machinery root publishes through its family singleflight (`execute_via_cold_build_helper_capturing_publication`). That publish is the component's linearization point: it represents a successfully completed result whose read set, self-roots and generation stamp are already validated.
- **Member publication is INDEPENDENTLY FENCED BACKFILL.** `relation_drain_completed_members` / `flow_return_drain_completed_members` / `resolve_call_drain_completed_members` run strictly AFTER that commit and hand each member to `publish_{relation,flow_return,resolve_call}_member_fenced`, which re-checks cancellation and the cold-abort sweep at its own publish. A member the fence refuses releases its inline flight, stays COLD, and recomputes on the next demand. Reduced cache completeness after the commit boundary is not corrupted semantics — every member is separately validated and separately recomputable.

Two things are NOT weakened by that split, and both admit nothing at all:

- **Pre-linearization cancellation** — a component cancelled before the root's admitted publish releases every flight without publishing anything.
- **Genuine component failure** — any degraded / `Unknown` / budget-exceeded / abandoned-session member poisons the WHOLE component: `ReturnOnly`, no entry, no fact signature, no reverse-index metadata, for the root and every member alike.

There is deliberately no retrospective rollback of a committed root when a later member is refused: rolling back would alter established relation semantics without adding correctness, because the refused member is never readable as a stale value — it is simply absent.

Guards: `mixed_component_member_publish_is_fenced_backfill_behind_a_committed_root`, `pre_linearization_cancellation_admits_nothing`, `genuine_component_failure_admits_neither_root_nor_member` (`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_tests.rs`).

## Template class fact demand

Dynamic `:class` type decisions belong to
`project_semantic_dispatch/template_class_facts.rs`, never to display text or
eager script-analysis DTOs. Select subjects from `RawTemplateData`, join them
to exact prepared binding keys or macro-payload locators, and classify every
union arm through the shared graph. Preserve wrapper carriers until the
requested value's producer-authored `AuthoredReferenceHeadFact` resolves
through shared import/export and local-alias facts to a package-backed terminal
whose final import edge is exactly `vue`. Terminal-instantiation demand
supplies fully substituted wrapper arguments; never classify an outer alias's
positional arguments. Any open or partial arm produces no class members.

The neutral artifact is revision-stamped and dependency-signed. Consumers use
the opaque session `TemplateClassDomainIndex`; do not reintroduce raw
`(binding, classes)` projections or type-annotation parsing.

## Reactive-wrapper demand (shared vocabulary)

`project_semantic_dispatch/reactive_wrapper.rs` is the ONE owner of the question
"does this authored reference head resolve to a reactive wrapper exported by the
`vue` package?". It owns `WrapperCandidate`, the exact route gate
`wrapper_candidate_for_route` (terminal import source is exactly `vue` **and**
`ResolverContext::workspace_is_package_backed`), and the closed vocabulary
`wrapper_role_for_vue_export` (`Ref` / `ShallowRef` / `ComputedRef` — with
`WritableComputedRef` normalizing onto it — / `ModelRef` / `Reactive` /
`ShallowReactive`). Template-class classification and the value-signature return
position both consume those items; a second copy is a one-engine violation.

An alternative whose sequential conjunction has no surviving declared arm is represented as impossible and contributes no overlay to the disjunction (`N23_impossible_conjunction_drops_dead_disjunction_alternative`). This is one `And`/`Or` authority consumed in positive and negative modes, not two pattern-specific rewrites.
- **Guaranteed-return qualifier for labelled-break inference.** In the preceding abrupt-edge rule, a “following current-function return” means a suffix statement that guarantees the return on every normal path (a direct return, a sequential block containing one, or both arms of an `if`). The qualifier is inherited through recursively lowered blocks and labels: an abrupt `finally` retains a pending named break as a return-inference-only suffix edge when the crossed target carries it. A suffix contributor already strictly covered by an ordinary return is redundant; an incomparable suffix remains in the inferred union. Merely containing a conditional return does not suppress the implicit-`undefined` contributor.
- **The root-identifier gate.** The shared shallow-pass leaf lowering (`infer_declaration_expression_type`) has NO frame — it resolves every name it meets in FILE OWNER SCOPE. So every leaf answer the slice content mints routes through ONE gate (`flow_slice_content.rs` — `Lowerer::leaf_type`, the sole producer of a leaf answer). Two evidence sources, one verdict: (a) the ANSWER's names, read off the produced typed IR through the shared exhaustive walk `verter_type_expr::referenced_names` (`typeof x…` value-path roots + named type references — never a re-derivation of the leaf's own traversal), and (b) for an answer the leaf could not model at all (a bare `any`), the expression's REFERENCE-CHAIN root (`a`, `a.b`, `a["b"]`, `a.#b`, `a?.b`, `a.b()`, `new a()`, `` a`…` ``, through parentheses and TS wrappers). A frame-owned name in (b) fails closed immediately (`SliceExpr::UnmodeledBinding` — no answer exists and no owner scope could supply one; POSITIONALLY, as the typed unresolved marker). A frame-owned name in (a) rides the `SliceExpr::FrameShadowed { inner, shadowed }` carrier, and the EVALUATOR decides against the live owner scope (`flow_return.rs` — the one shared `owner_scope_answers_frame_name` probe, taken through the same lowering the answer itself would take: `typeof name` for a value reference, a bare `name` reference for a type or namespace one; the head of `N.B` is the same scope lookup as a bare `N`, so the meanings differ on the FRAME side, not here): a name the owner scope ANSWERS fails closed positionally (the marker + `UnmodeledPosition`), a name it answers nothing for evaluates the wrapped leaf unchanged, because nothing can be mis-bound and the leaf's own typed miss is the honest result. Without the gate, `class CBait { static s = 1 } return CBait.s` published the module-scope `CBait`'s type, and `{ ...param }` / `param.m()` / `[localConst]` / `c ? localConst : 2` published the module-scope homonym's — cleanly and WARM. The `any`-half deliberately does NOT scan the whole subtree: a name in a position the leaf never consumes (a conditional TEST in `c ? 1 : 2`, an assignment target in `{ a: (x = "s") }`, a call argument) says nothing about the answer.
- **The frame gate covers every `TypeExpr` ENTRANCE, not just leaves — structurally.** Slice content mints types at eight `TypeExpr`-bearing fields, and each one is a place the frame-less shallow pass can hand back an owner-scope answer for a frame-owned name. Six of them (`SliceParam.ty` from an annotation, from a rest annotation, and from a default-initializer inference; `SliceTypeParam.constraint` / `.default`; `SliceStatement::Binding.declared`) hold the `GatedType` newtype (`flow_slice_content.rs`), whose `ty` / `shadowed` fields are PRIVATE and whose only two constructors are `Lowerer::gate` and the explicitly-named `GatedType::root_signature` — so "mint a slice-content type without deciding what the frame does to it" does not compile. The remaining two (`SliceExpr::Type` / `SliceCall::Symbolic`) ride the `SliceExpr::FrameShadowed` carrier from `Lowerer::leaf_type`, which additionally needs the `FrameShadowedRoot` `any`-arm annotations do not. The two free producers `lower_params` / `lower_slice_type_params` take a NON-defaultable `SignatureScope::{Root, Nested}`, so a new call site must choose the scope. `SliceStatement::Binding.declared` must be gated on the ANNOTATION itself: with a non-union declared type the evaluator binds the declared node and never evaluates the initializer, so the initializer's own gate cannot stand in.
- **Root signature vs nested signature (`resolveName`, `lastLocation !== location.body`).** A function's body-local type declarations are in scope ONLY inside its own body — never in its own parameter list, type-parameter clause, or parameter defaults (TypeScript discards a Type-meaning hit in a function-like `location`'s `locals` when `lastLocation !== location.body`; the value side mirrors it in `useOuterVariableScopeInParameter`). So the ROOT function's signature stays UNGATED (`SignatureScope::Root` ⇒ `GatedType::root_signature`) while a NESTED function value's signature — which sits inside the enclosing body — is gated against the ENCLOSING frame at the nested value's own span (`SignatureScope::Nested`). Gating the root positions would fail closed on `function f(p: Info) { class Info {} … }`, where the OUTER `Info` is correct. A parameter DEFAULT initializer additionally carries its reference-chain root as a `FrameShadowedName::Value`: a widened or primitive answer (`p = C` ⇒ `string`) names nothing at all while still having read THROUGH a frame binding.
- **A nested signature's OWN type parameters are BINDERS, in TYPE meaning only.** They are the names the evaluator's nested `flow_binder_env` interns, so an answer naming one resolves to the binder and a captured same-named `class` / `enum` does not shadow it (`Lowerer::name_is_frame_bound` subtracts them). In NAMESPACE meaning the binder still wins lexically but denotes no namespace, so a qualified `T.B` is unresolvable and stays frame-bound (fail-closed). The SHARED walk `verter_type_expr::referenced_names` masks the same class structurally: a `Function` / `ConstructorType` / method / call-signature node opens a binder frame over its own subtree on the same explicit heap work-stack the rest of the walk uses (depth-safe, exhaustive), so a generic function type in an ANSWER never reports its own `<T>` as a scope reference.
- **Type-space lookups are MEANING-filtered, and the meaning is per OCCURRENCE.** A bare `N` reference demands a `Type` meaning; the HEAD of a qualified `N.B` demands a `Namespace` meaning (`SymbolFlags.Namespace = ValueModule | NamespaceModule | Enum` — a class is NOT in it). `FunctionBodySkeleton::declares_meaning_in_scope(name, region, NameMeaning)` walks the region chain filtering by `SkeletonBindingKind::declares(meaning)` at EVERY hop (a scope whose symbol lacks the meaning is skipped and the walk continues outward), and `bindings_of_name_in_scope` is symmetric — it filters by `SkeletonBindingKind::declares_value()` at every hop, so the TYPE-ONLY kinds are transparent to a value lookup. Oracle-anchored cells (`tsc --strict`, one fixture per cell): `class` (± statics) and `type` / `interface` shadow the bare reference but NOT the qualified head; `namespace` is the reverse; `enum` / `const enum` shadow both; every value-only kind (`const` / `let` / `var` / `function` / parameter / catch-param) shadows neither; `class N` + `namespace N` shadows both while `function N` + `namespace N` shadows only the head. `import N = …` is meaning-TRANSPARENT (it occupies exactly its target's spaces), which the skeleton cannot decide, so it answers BOTH conservatively — a recorded over-fire that can only fail closed. The `qualified` bit rides `verter_type_expr::ReferencedTypeName` PER OCCURRENCE, because one answer can reference the same head both ways. `CaptureScope` therefore carries `type_names` and `namespace_names` as two SEPARATE inventories, and `FrameShadowedName` splits `Type` / `Namespace` alongside `Value`.
- **A named function expression's own name is a binding of its OWN frame.** `FunctionBodySource::from_function_expression` carries the expression's `id` into the nested `FunctionBodySkeleton` as a `SkeletonBindingKind::NestedFunction` binding of the ROOT region, so `const g = function h() { … h … }` resolves `h` through the nested frame's lexical authority (fail-closed, like every nested function declaration) instead of looking FREE and escaping to an enclosing or module-scope `h`. A function DECLARATION keeps `from_function` — its name binds in the ENCLOSING scope. Consequently `SliceCall::DirectSelf` is minted only where the frame owns a flow slot: `FlowEvaluator::self_slot` is `Option<&FlowReturnKey>` and is `None` inside every nested function value, so an inner self-call can no longer take a hold on the ENCLOSING function's slot.
- **A block-level function declaration is BLOCK-scoped.** `FunctionBodySkeleton::hoisting_bindings_of_name` hoists `SkeletonBindingKind::Var` unconditionally but a `NestedFunction` only when its recorded region is the frame's ROOT region: in strict-mode ESM (every carrier surface this substrate serves) a block-level function declaration is block-scoped, and only Annex-B sloppy-mode semantics create the function-scoped alias. Hoisting it unconditionally made `if (c) { function f() {…} } return f()` resolve to the block's function and FAIL CLOSED where the correct answer is the module-scope `f`'s return. (Latent, no live consumer: `StatementListInventory.nested_function_names` in `function_program.rs` carries no region axis.)
- **The interim `DirectCall` annotation rail (final semantics: U6.CALL_RESOLVE).** A value declaration carrying BOTH an authored annotation and an initializer is typed by the ANNOTATION — the initializer only has to be assignable to it. The direct-call rail therefore checks the target's prepared value decl for an authored annotation (`ValueAnnotationClass::Direct` / `TypeOfAlias` with a `SemanticTypeSource::Authored` source) and, when present, resolves the callee as a VALUE TYPE through the same shared path a parenthesised or ambient callee takes (`call_return_of_callee_node`), never through the initializer's own flow position: `const f: () => 42 = () => 42; f()` is `42`, not the initializer arrow's inferred `number`. FINAL declarator-annotated call semantics are owned by `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`; this rail is the interim HONEST answer, not the finished mechanism.
- **A CALLEE's own clause instantiates AT THE CALL SITE, on every route (sb15).** Whatever a callee answers with — its body-derived flow return, its DECLARED return carrier, or a resolved signature node's return position — is expressed in the CALLEE's own type-parameter binders, so handing it back verbatim publishes the callee's generic parameter as the caller's whole-function return, cleanly and warm. That is unsound rather than merely imprecise, because the evaluator's binder identity is file-scoped and name-keyed (`DeclIdentity::from_scope(file_scope, name)`, `param_index: 0`): an enclosing `class Holder<T>` and a same-named callee parameter intern to ONE `SemanticNodeId`, so the leaked binder is substitutable by an instantiation that has nothing to do with it (`new Holder<number>().viaCall()` answering `number`).

  **The rule is structurally confined, not per-arm.** Every call form rides ONE `SliceExpr::Call(SliceCall, SliceCallSite)` carrier over a closed six-variant vocabulary (`Nested` / `OnBinding` / `LocalFunctionShadow` / `DirectSelf` / `Direct` / `Symbolic`, `flow_slice_content.rs`), and the evaluator answers them in ONE exhaustive `FlowEvaluator::eval_call` whose sink type is `CallValue` (`project_semantic_dispatch::flow_return_callee`). **That closes the call VOCABULARY; whether a call REACHES it is the content lowering's separate obligation, and it is held by two more rails.** Expression-form exhaustiveness lives in the SHARED classifier `analysis::flow::value_descent`, not in `Lowerer::lower_expr`: `lower_expr` handles the frame-local carriers (identifier, nested function value, call) and ends in `other => match value_descent(other)`, and it is the classifier's wildcard-free match over `Expression` that refuses to compile for a new variant — which is what makes the disposition binding on the demand PLANNER as well (see the `FunctionBodySkeleton` bullet). A wildcard is what let a CONDITIONAL expression sit silently in the leaf list, folding `return c ? f() : g()` through the frame-less shallow pass into an unreduced `ReturnType<callee>` carrier that was published warm with the callee's own binders intact and its overload group unconsulted, while the `if` / `return` twin of the same body went through `SliceCall` and degraded correctly. A conditional is now a `ValueDescent::Branches` disposition (`SliceExpr::Union` over both branch values, joined through the same normalizing interner the contributor join uses), and a leaf answer that EMBEDS the shallow pass's own call-return carrier (`type_eval_build::embeds_call_return_carrier`, read through the shared exhaustive `referenced_names` walk, the predicate colocated with the ONE site that mints the carrier) is `SliceExpr::UnreducedCallValue` and takes the POSITIONAL disposition — the typed unresolved marker contributed AT the position with `FlowReturnDegradation::UnmodeledPosition` recorded — never a published carrier holding a foreign binder, and never a discarded composite. **That carrier gate alone was narrower than the promise it delivered, and the gap is now closed at the FORM rather than at the answer.** The shallow pass's per-expression lowering ends in `_ => Ok(Primitive(Any))` and `lower_leaf`'s `is_any` arm runs BEFORE the carrier gate, so a form whose leaf answer is a bare `any` never reached the gate at all — `new f()`, `` tag`…` ``, `f?.()`, `await f()`, `(k, f())`, `f()!`, `this.m()`, `super.m()` and an unrepresentable computed callee (`obj[sym]()`) all published a fabricated `any` cleanly and warm under a promise that a call with no structural arm fails closed. The call-position verdict is now the classifier's `ValueDescent::UnmodeledCall` (predicate `analysis::flow::value_is_unmodeled_call`, the single authority both `value_descent` and `lower_leaf`'s residual type-carrier check delegate to), plus the `CallExpression` arm's own unrepresentable-callee case, so every one of those fails closed POSITIONALLY whatever the shallow pass answered. **The line is FABRICATION, not the form's own value.** The earlier line — "the form's OWN value IS a call's return" — left every JOIN (`k || f()`, `k ?? f()`), PROJECTION (`f().q`, `f()["q"]`, `f?.()?.q`), OPERATOR (`f() + "x"`), ASSIGNMENT (`z = f()`) and ARRAY-ELEMENT (`["s", new Box()]`) form publishing the shallow pass's fabricated `any`, clean and warm. It was justified as "`any` is UNDER the checker's answer, never over it". That justification is UNSOUND: `any` is BIDIRECTIONALLY assignable, so it is neither under nor over — it silences every check in both directions and is indistinguishable from an authored `any` at every downstream gate. Being under the checker was never the property that made a value publishable; being DISTINGUISHABLE from a known one is. The gate is now `leaf_answer_is_fabricated_at_a_call_position` (`flow_slice_content.rs`): the answer embeds the call-return carrier, OR the answer embeds `any` AND `analysis::flow::value_composes_unmodeled_call` says the expression's value composes over a call with no structural arm. The conjunction is what prevents over-refusal — a form whose answer the pass DOES model (`f() === 1` is `boolean`, `f() as T` is `T`) embeds no `any` and passes, and an AUTHORED `any` (`x as any`) composes no call and passes. `AssignmentExpression` is in `value_is_unmodeled_call` for the same reason `SequenceExpression` is: an assignment's value IS its right-hand side. A JSX attribute's call is likewise NOT routed here: a JSX element's value is `JSX.Element` and does not depend on any attribute's value, so the element's `any` is the shallow pass's fallback row, not a call position. Acceptance: `an_unmodeled_call_position_fails_closed_whatever_the_shallow_pass_answered` + `non_call_forms_and_modeled_call_arms_are_untouched_by_the_call_position_gate` + `flow_return_leaf_answered_call_forms_publish_any_not_a_carrier` (the recorded boundary table). Closing the shallow pass's `_ => Any` disposition is `U6.VALUE_INFERENCE` debt (row FR-D4 below), not this rail's. `CallValue`'s field is PRIVATE and every constructor lives in that module, so "hand a callee's return back untouched" does not compile at a call site — the no-op is reachable only by naming a NON-GENERIC `CalleeClause` (`CalleeClause::non_generic`), a statement about the callee rather than an omission. `CalleeClause` is deliberately NOT `Default`, and a route that cannot READ the clause cannot mint one — STRUCTURALLY: `CalleeClause::non_generic` / `::new` and `CalleeClauseParam::bare` / `::with_default` are all PRIVATE to `flow_return_callee.rs`, so the three fabrications a reviewer planted (`non_generic()` on a serve miss, `new(iter::empty())` on an index miss, `new([bare("Invented")])` from nothing) now fail to compile with `E0624` instead of building clean. The two clause entrances each demand the callee's own AUTHORITY as an argument: `CalleeClause::read_from_program_entry` (the call-site rule) and `read_from_program_entry_at_unknown` (the signature-UTILITY policy) take a `FunctionProgramMatch` — a private-field witness minted ONLY by a keyed lookup on a `FunctionProgramIndex` (`get` / `value_function` / `matches_named`); `CallValue::of_signature_node` reads the clause off a resolved `Signature` node. A bare `&FunctionProgramEntry` was NOT that witness, though the module doc claimed the reference itself was proof of a successful lookup. Two defeats compiled against it, and closing only the obvious one would have left the dangerous one: a struct literal assembled out of nothing (now blocked because `FunctionProgramEntry` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so no other crate can construct one by literal OR by `Clone` + functional update), and — the realistic one — an index MISS falling back to `index.entries.first()`, handing the reader a genuine entry for the WRONG callee and reading that callee's clause as this one's. `FunctionProgramIndex::entries` is private with no positional accessor, so every way out of the index NAMES the position it wants; the two plants now fail with `E0639` / `E0308` and `E0616` respectively. What remains a convention, deliberately, is that the caller looks up the callee it meant: a witness for a deliberately-wrong KEY is still a witness, and binding the key to the callee's identity end-to-end is `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`'s. A serve or index miss has nothing to hand over and returns `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable` (or `None`), which routes to the `UnrepresentableCallee` degradation. The two routes are now SYMMETRIC on a miss: `instantiate_callee_clause_at_unknown` used to return the callee's body-derived return UNTOUCHED — its own binders published warm — where the call-site route degraded on the identical miss. Collapsing that into "the callee is not generic" is how a lookup FAILURE hands the callee's return back verbatim, binders and all, with no degradation and full warm admission. The SCC fixed point is confined the same way: a hold carries its callee's clause (`HeldCallee`), and `HeldCallee::discharged` is the only accessor turning a hold target's admitted result into a join arm, so the equation cannot re-run the transfer around the gate. Exactly one exemption exists and is named: `HeldCallee::own_frame`, the direct SELF-call, whose callee IS the calling frame — its binders are the frame's own and must survive (`f<T>(x: T): T` stays `T`, not `T | unknown`).

  The route inventory, all gated: (1) a resolved callee VALUE TYPE (`call_return_of_callee_node`, reached from the annotated-declarator direct call and from the symbolic `ReturnType<typeof …>` carrier); (2) an IIFE's inline nested signature; (3) a call on a function-typed local / parameter / captured BINDING; (4) a direct call's body-derived FLOW return; (5) a direct call's DECLARED return carrier; (6) the SCC fixed-point discharge. Routes (1)–(3) read the clause off the signature node itself (`CallValue::of_signature_node`); routes (4)–(6) take it as a `CalleeClause` because the flow rail's callee answers with a bare return node and never composes a signature.

  A SEVENTH consumer takes a value from a callee's return position without being a CALL at all: `flow_return_member_projection` (`walk.rs` → `flow_return.rs`), the path-precise `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` rail. It is the signature-UTILITY policy, not the call policy — `ReturnType<…>` has no call site to be argument-free at, so every free clause parameter instantiates at `unknown` and a declared default never applies (`ReturnType<typeof f>` and `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` over `f<MG = number>(x: MG)` are both `unknown`-valued, checker-verified). It applies that policy through `instantiate_named_params_at_unknown` over clause NAMES read from the shallow `FunctionProgramIndex`, NOT by composing the callee's signature: a whole-signature composition here would materialise exactly the sibling members the member demand exists to leave cold. Returning the demand's return position RAW published the callee's own binder as the consumer's value, and made the whole-return route and its one-segment-longer sibling disagree about one callee.

  Four details make it hold. (a) The flow rail's clause is read from the per-file `FunctionProgramIndex` entry's `type_parameters`, keyed by the target's exact program identity, NOT from the prepared value declaration — the value registry does not carry a namespace-scoped function at all, and reading the clause there leaves exactly those callees leaking. (b) The name-driven binder collection can claim THREE resolution states of one clause parameter — the bound `TypeParam`, the deferred `BareRef`, and the RESOLVED `DeclRef` — and WHICH of them it claims is chosen per route by `ClauseSpelling`, because the answer depends on PROVENANCE and the name alone cannot supply it. A declaration's own parameter is not in scope where its DECLARED return locator lowers (file owner scope), so `f<T>(): T` interns its return as an unbound `BareRef("T")`, and when the file ALSO declares a type named `T` that owner-scope lowering RESOLVES the head to the wrong symbol (`interface Item {}` beside `function first<Item>(xs: Item[]): Item`) — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithOwnerScopeResolution`, used by routes whose node came from an owner-scope-lowered declared return (the direct call's DECLARED carrier, and the resolved callee VALUE TYPE). A BODY-DERIVED return is the opposite case: it is evaluated in the callee's own frame where the clause IS bound, so its parameters are already `TypeParam` binders and a resolved `DeclRef` reached through such an arm is by construction a DIFFERENT symbol — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithDeferredHeads`, used by the flow rail, the SCC discharge, an IIFE's composed signature, and the function-typed BINDING route (`SliceCall::OnBinding`). The binding route is the one that has to be argued rather than read off the carrier: a binding's value is either a composed signature (built in the callee's own frame) or a `<T>(x: T) => T` annotation (lowered with its clause in scope), so BOTH spell the clause as binders, and the one shape that could carry an owner-scope misresolution — `typeof declaredFn` — never reaches a `Signature` node on that route at all (it resolves to a non-callable surface and takes the `NonCallableBinding` degradation). Spelling it owner-scope-declared therefore buys nothing and costs a correct arm, and the discriminator is that the SAME callee body reached two ways must answer once: `const g = <NB,>(j) => (j ? nbValue : null); return g(true)` and the immediately-invoked twin both keep the file-scope `interface NB` the callee's own clause never shadows. A NAME-scoped claim erases exactly-correct arms: `aye<QQ>(x, f) { if (f) return bee(); return x; }` beside `interface QQ` and `bee(): QQ` answers `1 | QQ`, and the name-only claim republished it as `unknown | unknown`. A NON-generic callee returning the same interface publishes its `DeclRef` untouched on either route. (c) A parameter carrying a DECLARED DEFAULT instantiates to that default ONLY when inference could produce no candidate — TypeScript takes the default exactly when inference produced none (`checker.ts::getInferredTypes`), so `f<T = number>()` IS `number` while `f<T = string>(x: T)` called `f(1)` is `number`, NOT `string`. Applying it unconditionally turns the honest interim (`unknown`, for the inference this substrate does not model) into a confidently WRONG concrete type, warm-admitted. The rule is expressed on the two facts `SliceCallSite` carries — an argument count (spread-aware) and an explicit-type-arguments flag — plus the shallow `FunctionProgramTypeParam::first_parameter_occurrence` (the smallest formal-parameter ordinal whose authored type names the parameter, shadow-aware): explicit type arguments ⇒ `unknown`; else an occurrence at a SUPPLIED ordinal ⇒ `unknown`; else the declared default, else `unknown`. That is why `f<T = number>(x: string)` and `f<T = number>(a: string, b?: T)` still take their default at an argument-BEARING call, both checker-verified. The default TYPES are a body lowering demanded through `DeclBodyMemo::function_type_param_clause`, only for parameters the rule actually needs one for, so an ordinary generic callee — and a defaulted parameter the call infers — pays nothing; a needed default that cannot be recovered is `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable`, never a fabricated `unknown`. A default naming a sibling parameter instantiates in turn (`<A, B = A>` answers `unknown`, never `A`). The signature-UTILITY entrance keeps `unknown` regardless of defaults, because `ReturnType<typeof f>` for `f<T = number>(): T` is `unknown` — the two entrances are deliberately separate (`instantiate_clause_params_at_call` vs `instantiate_free_signature_params_at_unknown`). (d) An OVERLOADED callee is NOT answerable at a call site, and the predicate is the SIZE of the overload group ALONE. TypeScript picks the FIRST signature whose parameters accept the arguments; the direct rail reaches one `FunctionProgramIndex` entry per group (the trailing IMPLEMENTATION, exactly what overload visibility HIDES), and the resolved-callee rail reaches `select_signature_function`, which deliberately selects the LAST signature because that is what the signature UTILITIES want. Gating on "the selected signature has an implementation body" therefore closed only the BODIED half: an AMBIENT group (`declare function f(…)` ×3, no implementation at all) published the LAST declaration's return where the language answers the first, cleanly and warm. Both rails now degrade on group size — the direct rail on `prepared.signatures.len() > 1`, the resolved-callee rail on `signature_bucket_arity(.., Call) > 1` — to `UnrepresentableCallee` (usable modeled `any`, `ReturnOnly` by contract). `select_signature_function` is UNCHANGED, so `ReturnType<typeof overloaded>` still reads the last overload. A LONE signature is untouched, bodied or not. **METHOD-position groups reach that gate too.** A surface RETAINS every same-name method contributor, but `SurfaceView::project_known_key` is first-wins — right for a property, silently truncating for an overload set — so `objOv.m(1)` over `{ m(x: string): "PA"; m(x: number): "PB" }` published `"PA"` warm where the language answers `"PB"`, and `signature_bucket_arity` saw one signature where there are two. Four shapes were affected (class method, object-type method, interface method, and a method reached through an INTERSECTION arm). The shared PathWalker's Object hop now asks `SurfaceView::project_known_key_overload_group` first: two or more PUBLIC same-key members that are ALL `ObjectMethodKind::Method` project as the canonical overload-group carrier — an object whose CALL SIGNATURES are the contributors — so the existing size gate sees the real arity. A lone method and a plain property keep their exact first-wins answer. **The carrier applies overload VISIBILITY, and the two producers share ONE rule rather than agreeing by convention.** As first landed it did not: it filtered on `visibility.is_public() && method_kind == Method` and stopped, while `build_typeof` additionally HIDES the trailing implementation signature of a multi-signature group — the filter `select_signature_function` documents as its PRECONDITION before reading the LAST overload. So for a group WITH an implementation the last overload WAS the implementation: `OvImpl['m']` published three signatures including `(x: any): any` where the checker publishes two, `ReturnType<OvImpl['m']>` became `any` (checker `"MB"`) and `Parameters<…>` became `[x: any]` (checker `[x: number]`) — cleanly, warm, on the SHARED PathWalker hop component-meta's published prop types travel. Every overload fixture that shipped with the carrier was implementation-free, so the suite structurally could not catch it. The rule now has one home, `semantic_query::visible_overload_ordinals` (surface every BODILESS contributor in source order; if none, surface all — which covers the lone-bodied signature without a special case), and BOTH producers call it, so "byte-identical in shape to what `build_typeof` mints" is true by construction rather than by review. Acceptance: `method_overload_group_carrier_hides_the_implementation_signature`, `visible_overload_ordinals_covers_every_group_shape`.

Call-site instantiation proper, and overload resolution, are `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`'s; sb15 IS the checker's answer for the one shape TS itself cannot infer (`bare<T>(): T` called with no arguments is `unknown`), and a declared default is exact.
