  **The rule is structurally confined, not per-arm.** Every call form rides ONE `SliceExpr::Call(SliceCall, SliceCallSite)` carrier over a closed six-variant vocabulary (`Nested` / `OnBinding` / `LocalFunctionShadow` / `DirectSelf` / `Direct` / `Symbolic`, `flow_slice_content.rs`), and the evaluator answers them in ONE exhaustive `FlowEvaluator::eval_call` whose sink type is `CallValue` (`project_semantic_dispatch::flow_return_callee`). **That closes the call VOCABULARY; whether a call REACHES it is the content lowering's separate obligation, and it is held by two more rails.** Expression-form exhaustiveness lives in the SHARED classifier `analysis::flow::value_descent`, not in `Lowerer::lower_expr`: `lower_expr` handles the frame-local carriers (identifier, nested function value, call) and ends in `other => match value_descent(other)`, and it is the classifier's wildcard-free match over `Expression` that refuses to compile for a new variant — which is what makes the disposition binding on the demand PLANNER as well (see the `FunctionBodySkeleton` bullet). A wildcard is what let a CONDITIONAL expression sit silently in the leaf list, folding `return c ? f() : g()` through the frame-less shallow pass into an unreduced `ReturnType<callee>` carrier that was published warm with the callee's own binders intact and its overload group unconsulted, while the `if` / `return` twin of the same body went through `SliceCall` and degraded correctly. A conditional is now a `ValueDescent::Branches` disposition (`SliceExpr::Union` over both branch values, joined through the same normalizing interner the contributor join uses), and a leaf answer that EMBEDS the shallow pass's own call-return carrier (`type_eval_build::embeds_call_return_carrier`, read through the shared exhaustive `referenced_names` walk, the predicate colocated with the ONE site that mints the carrier) is `SliceExpr::UnreducedCallValue` and takes the POSITIONAL disposition — the typed unresolved marker contributed AT the position with `FlowReturnDegradation::UnmodeledPosition` recorded — never a published carrier holding a foreign binder, and never a discarded composite. **That carrier gate alone was narrower than the promise it delivered, and the gap is now closed at the FORM rather than at the answer.** The shallow pass's per-expression lowering ends in `_ => Ok(Primitive(Any))` and `lower_leaf`'s `is_any` arm runs BEFORE the carrier gate, so a form whose leaf answer is a bare `any` never reached the gate at all — `new f()`, `` tag`…` ``, `f?.()`, `await f()`, `(k, f())`, `f()!`, `this.m()`, `super.m()` and an unrepresentable computed callee (`obj[sym]()`) all published a fabricated `any` cleanly and warm under a promise that a call with no structural arm fails closed. The call-position verdict is now the classifier's `ValueDescent::UnmodeledCall` (predicate `analysis::flow::value_is_unmodeled_call`, the single authority both `value_descent` and `lower_leaf`'s residual type-carrier check delegate to), plus the `CallExpression` arm's own unrepresentable-callee case, so every one of those fails closed POSITIONALLY whatever the shallow pass answered. **The line is FABRICATION, not the form's own value.** The earlier line — "the form's OWN value IS a call's return" — left every JOIN (`k || f()`, `k ?? f()`), PROJECTION (`f().q`, `f()["q"]`, `f?.()?.q`), OPERATOR (`f() + "x"`), ASSIGNMENT (`z = f()`) and ARRAY-ELEMENT (`["s", new Box()]`) form publishing the shallow pass's fabricated `any`, clean and warm. It was justified as "`any` is UNDER the checker's answer, never over it". That justification is UNSOUND: `any` is BIDIRECTIONALLY assignable, so it is neither under nor over — it silences every check in both directions and is indistinguishable from an authored `any` at every downstream gate. Being under the checker was never the property that made a value publishable; being DISTINGUISHABLE from a known one is. The gate is now `leaf_answer_is_fabricated_at_a_call_position` (`flow_slice_content.rs`): the answer embeds the call-return carrier, OR the answer embeds `any` AND `analysis::flow::value_composes_unmodeled_call` says the expression's value composes over a call with no structural arm. The conjunction is what prevents over-refusal — a form whose answer the pass DOES model (`f() === 1` is `boolean`, `f() as T` is `T`) embeds no `any` and passes, and an AUTHORED `any` (`x as any`) composes no call and passes. `AssignmentExpression` is in `value_is_unmodeled_call` for the same reason `SequenceExpression` is: an assignment's value IS its right-hand side. A JSX attribute's call is likewise NOT routed here: a JSX element's value is `JSX.Element` and does not depend on any attribute's value, so the element's `any` is the shallow pass's fallback row, not a call position. Acceptance: `an_unmodeled_call_position_fails_closed_whatever_the_shallow_pass_answered` + `non_call_forms_and_modeled_call_arms_are_untouched_by_the_call_position_gate` + `flow_return_leaf_answered_call_forms_publish_any_not_a_carrier` (the recorded boundary table). Closing the shallow pass's `_ => Any` disposition is `U6.VALUE_INFERENCE` debt (row FR-D4 below), not this rail's. `CallValue`'s field is PRIVATE and every constructor lives in that module, so "hand a callee's return back untouched" does not compile at a call site — the no-op is reachable only by naming a NON-GENERIC `CalleeClause` (`CalleeClause::non_generic`), a statement about the callee rather than an omission. `CalleeClause` is deliberately NOT `Default`, and a route that cannot READ the clause cannot mint one — STRUCTURALLY: `CalleeClause::non_generic` / `::new` and `CalleeClauseParam::bare` / `::with_default` are all PRIVATE to `flow_return_callee.rs`, so the three fabrications a reviewer planted (`non_generic()` on a serve miss, `new(iter::empty())` on an index miss, `new([bare("Invented")])` from nothing) now fail to compile with `E0624` instead of building clean. The two clause entrances each demand the callee's own AUTHORITY as an argument: `CalleeClause::read_from_program_entry` (the call-site rule) and `read_from_program_entry_at_unknown` (the signature-UTILITY policy) take a `FunctionProgramMatch` — a private-field witness minted ONLY by a keyed lookup on a `FunctionProgramIndex` (`get` / `value_function` / `matches_named`); `CallValue::of_signature_node` reads the clause off a resolved `Signature` node. A bare `&FunctionProgramEntry` was NOT that witness, though the module doc claimed the reference itself was proof of a successful lookup. Two defeats compiled against it, and closing only the obvious one would have left the dangerous one: a struct literal assembled out of nothing (now blocked because `FunctionProgramEntry` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so no other crate can construct one by literal OR by `Clone` + functional update), and — the realistic one — an index MISS falling back to `index.entries.first()`, handing the reader a genuine entry for the WRONG callee and reading that callee's clause as this one's. `FunctionProgramIndex::entries` is private with no positional accessor, so every way out of the index NAMES the position it wants; the two plants now fail with `E0639` / `E0308` and `E0616` respectively. What remains a convention, deliberately, is that the caller looks up the callee it meant: a witness for a deliberately-wrong KEY is still a witness, and binding the key to the callee's identity end-to-end is `U6.CALL_RESOLVE`'s. A serve or index miss has nothing to hand over and returns `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable` (or `None`), which routes to the `UnrepresentableCallee` degradation. The two routes are now SYMMETRIC on a miss: `instantiate_callee_clause_at_unknown` used to return the callee's body-derived return UNTOUCHED — its own binders published warm — where the call-site route degraded on the identical miss. Collapsing that into "the callee is not generic" is how a lookup FAILURE hands the callee's return back verbatim, binders and all, with no degradation and full warm admission. The SCC fixed point is confined the same way: a hold carries its callee's clause (`HeldCallee`), and `HeldCallee::discharged` is the only accessor turning a hold target's admitted result into a join arm, so the equation cannot re-run the transfer around the gate. Exactly one exemption exists and is named: `HeldCallee::own_frame`, the direct SELF-call, whose callee IS the calling frame — its binders are the frame's own and must survive (`f<T>(x: T): T` stays `T`, not `T | unknown`).

  The route inventory, all gated: (1) a resolved callee VALUE TYPE (`call_return_of_callee_node`, reached from the annotated-declarator direct call and from the symbolic `ReturnType<typeof …>` carrier); (2) an IIFE's inline nested signature; (3) a call on a function-typed local / parameter / captured BINDING; (4) a direct call's body-derived FLOW return; (5) a direct call's DECLARED return carrier; (6) the SCC fixed-point discharge. Routes (1)–(3) read the clause off the signature node itself (`CallValue::of_signature_node`); routes (4)–(6) take it as a `CalleeClause` because the flow rail's callee answers with a bare return node and never composes a signature.

  A SEVENTH consumer takes a value from a callee's return position without being a CALL at all: `flow_return_member_projection` (`walk.rs` → `flow_return.rs`), the path-precise `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` rail. It is the signature-UTILITY policy, not the call policy — `ReturnType<…>` has no call site to be argument-free at, so every free clause parameter instantiates at `unknown` and a declared default never applies (`ReturnType<typeof f>` and `ReturnType<typeof f>['m']` over `f<MG = number>(x: MG)` are both `unknown`-valued, checker-verified). It applies that policy through `instantiate_named_params_at_unknown` over clause NAMES read from the shallow `FunctionProgramIndex`, NOT by composing the callee's signature: a whole-signature composition here would materialise exactly the sibling members the member demand exists to leave cold. Returning the demand's return position RAW published the callee's own binder as the consumer's value, and made the whole-return route and its one-segment-longer sibling disagree about one callee.

  Four details make it hold. (a) The flow rail's clause is read from the per-file `FunctionProgramIndex` entry's `type_parameters`, keyed by the target's exact program identity, NOT from the prepared value declaration — the value registry does not carry a namespace-scoped function at all, and reading the clause there leaves exactly those callees leaking. (b) The name-driven binder collection can claim THREE resolution states of one clause parameter — the bound `TypeParam`, the deferred `BareRef`, and the RESOLVED `DeclRef` — and WHICH of them it claims is chosen per route by `ClauseSpelling`, because the answer depends on PROVENANCE and the name alone cannot supply it. A declaration's own parameter is not in scope where its DECLARED return locator lowers (file owner scope), so `f<T>(): T` interns its return as an unbound `BareRef("T")`, and when the file ALSO declares a type named `T` that owner-scope lowering RESOLVES the head to the wrong symbol (`interface Item {}` beside `function first<Item>(xs: Item[]): Item`) — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithOwnerScopeResolution`, used by routes whose node came from an owner-scope-lowered declared return (the direct call's DECLARED carrier, and the resolved callee VALUE TYPE). A BODY-DERIVED return is the opposite case: it is evaluated in the callee's own frame where the clause IS bound, so its parameters are already `TypeParam` binders and a resolved `DeclRef` reached through such an arm is by construction a DIFFERENT symbol — that is `ClauseSpelling::WithDeferredHeads`, used by the flow rail, the SCC discharge, an IIFE's composed signature, and the function-typed BINDING route (`SliceCall::OnBinding`). The binding route is the one that has to be argued rather than read off the carrier: a binding's value is either a composed signature (built in the callee's own frame) or a `<T>(x: T) => T` annotation (lowered with its clause in scope), so BOTH spell the clause as binders, and the one shape that could carry an owner-scope misresolution — `typeof declaredFn` — never reaches a `Signature` node on that route at all (it resolves to a non-callable surface and takes the `NonCallableBinding` degradation). Spelling it owner-scope-declared therefore buys nothing and costs a correct arm, and the discriminator is that the SAME callee body reached two ways must answer once: `const g = <NB,>(j) => (j ? nbValue : null); return g(true)` and the immediately-invoked twin both keep the file-scope `interface NB` the callee's own clause never shadows. A NAME-scoped claim erases exactly-correct arms: `aye<QQ>(x, f) { if (f) return bee(); return x; }` beside `interface QQ` and `bee(): QQ` answers `1 | QQ`, and the name-only claim republished it as `unknown | unknown`. A NON-generic callee returning the same interface publishes its `DeclRef` untouched on either route. (c) A parameter carrying a DECLARED DEFAULT instantiates to that default ONLY when inference could produce no candidate — TypeScript takes the default exactly when inference produced none (`checker.ts::getInferredTypes`), so `f<T = number>()` IS `number` while `f<T = string>(x: T)` called `f(1)` is `number`, NOT `string`. Applying it unconditionally turns the honest interim (`unknown`, for the inference this substrate does not model) into a confidently WRONG concrete type, warm-admitted. The rule is expressed on the two facts `SliceCallSite` carries — an argument count (spread-aware) and an explicit-type-arguments flag — plus the shallow `FunctionProgramTypeParam::first_parameter_occurrence` (the smallest formal-parameter ordinal whose authored type names the parameter, shadow-aware): explicit type arguments ⇒ `unknown`; else an occurrence at a SUPPLIED ordinal ⇒ `unknown`; else the declared default, else `unknown`. That is why `f<T = number>(x: string)` and `f<T = number>(a: string, b?: T)` still take their default at an argument-BEARING call, both checker-verified. The default TYPES are a body lowering demanded through `DeclBodyMemo::function_type_param_clause`, only for parameters the rule actually needs one for, so an ordinary generic callee — and a defaulted parameter the call infers — pays nothing; a needed default that cannot be recovered is `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable`, never a fabricated `unknown`. A default naming a sibling parameter instantiates in turn (`<A, B = A>` answers `unknown`, never `A`). The signature-UTILITY entrance keeps `unknown` regardless of defaults, because `ReturnType<typeof f>` for `f<T = number>(): T` is `unknown` — the two entrances are deliberately separate (`instantiate_clause_params_at_call` vs `instantiate_free_signature_params_at_unknown`). (d) An OVERLOADED callee is NOT answerable at a call site, and the predicate is the SIZE of the overload group ALONE. TypeScript picks the FIRST signature whose parameters accept the arguments; the direct rail reaches one `FunctionProgramIndex` entry per group (the trailing IMPLEMENTATION, exactly what overload visibility HIDES), and the resolved-callee rail reaches `select_signature_function`, which deliberately selects the LAST signature because that is what the signature UTILITIES want. Gating on "the selected signature has an implementation body" therefore closed only the BODIED half: an AMBIENT group (`declare function f(…)` ×3, no implementation at all) published the LAST declaration's return where the language answers the first, cleanly and warm. Both rails now degrade on group size — the direct rail on `prepared.signatures.len() > 1`, the resolved-callee rail on `signature_bucket_arity(.., Call) > 1` — to `UnrepresentableCallee` (usable modeled `any`, `ReturnOnly` by contract). `select_signature_function` is UNCHANGED, so `ReturnType<typeof overloaded>` still reads the last overload. A LONE signature is untouched, bodied or not. **METHOD-position groups reach that gate too.** A surface RETAINS every same-name method contributor, but `SurfaceView::project_known_key` is first-wins — right for a property, silently truncating for an overload set — so `objOv.m(1)` over `{ m(x: string): "PA"; m(x: number): "PB" }` published `"PA"` warm where the language answers `"PB"`, and `signature_bucket_arity` saw one signature where there are two. Four shapes were affected (class method, object-type method, interface method, and a method reached through an INTERSECTION arm). The shared PathWalker's Object hop now asks `SurfaceView::project_known_key_overload_group` first: two or more PUBLIC same-key members that are ALL `ObjectMethodKind::Method` project as the canonical overload-group carrier — an object whose CALL SIGNATURES are the contributors — so the existing size gate sees the real arity. A lone method and a plain property keep their exact first-wins answer. **The carrier applies overload VISIBILITY, and the two producers share ONE rule rather than agreeing by convention.** As first landed it did not: it filtered on `visibility.is_public() && method_kind == Method` and stopped, while `build_typeof` additionally HIDES the trailing implementation signature of a multi-signature group — the filter `select_signature_function` documents as its PRECONDITION before reading the LAST overload. So for a group WITH an implementation the last overload WAS the implementation: `OvImpl['m']` published three signatures including `(x: any): any` where the checker publishes two, `ReturnType<OvImpl['m']>` became `any` (checker `"MB"`) and `Parameters<…>` became `[x: any]` (checker `[x: number]`) — cleanly, warm, on the SHARED PathWalker hop component-meta's published prop types travel. Every overload fixture that shipped with the carrier was implementation-free, so the suite structurally could not catch it. The rule now has one home, `semantic_query::visible_overload_ordinals` (surface every BODILESS contributor in source order; if none, surface all — which covers the lone-bodied signature without a special case), and BOTH producers call it, so "byte-identical in shape to what `build_typeof` mints" is true by construction rather than by review. Acceptance: `method_overload_group_carrier_hides_the_implementation_signature`, `visible_overload_ordinals_covers_every_group_shape`.

codex
The first correction is already emerging: the draft’s “one real load point” framing is too narrow. The shared resolver is demand-recursive—declaration-body lowering, cross-file route discovery, augmentation stitching, `typeof`, and semantic subqueries can all discover inputs below a top-level query. I’m now checking whether C2’s contract makes that breadth mandatory and whether crate privacy can prove the no-I/O property.

Maintainer ratified A5-L1/G1/DD1/R-12/S1 (loop5_instrumentation converge+delete owners G4/K3/L4; attribution/compile-fail locked as per-block commands, CI deferred post-program; verter_semantic->verter_workspace pinned exception, C1 removal gate; 469 unlanded local branches abandoned as a class; stack policy max_open_stack_layers=2/ATOMIC_REVIEW/LOCAL_BRANCH_CHAIN). docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:276:notes = "Gap-analysis-only block: every one of BF1's 7 numbered exit criteria and all owned-scope bullets independently verified already satisfied by the previously-landed, maintainer-ratified AMD-005 package. REOPEN #1 (legitimate, new finding not previously reviewed): the parallelism consult found exit criterion #6 (BF2 performance cells frozen before BF2 work begins) was unmet — performance-gates.toml had no BF2 cells. Resolved by measuring the already-authored, BF1-owned official-case enumeration tool (generate-official-case-manifests.mjs) against the pinned oracle sources — a legitimate before-BF2-exists reference measurement, not criterion-selection-after-candidate-measurement — freezing BF2_VUE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE/BF2_SVELTE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE (10-invocation session, wall/RSS bounds, SHA-256 output-oracle, exact-equality work counters, operationally-proven zero-network via a live curl-denial control). First review pass: architecture BLOCKING (cells mislabeled as covering golden/compiler-invocation generation, which was never measured); fixed by rescoping the operation text to enumeration/classification only and adding an explicit open/deferred row in performance-impact.md for the heavier compiler-invocation+golden workload (matching the existing BV1/BS1/B6/C4 deferred-row pattern). Reattested PASS, no threshold values changed, no scope creep. candidate_sha == accepted_sha exactly (no landing squash needed beyond the one already-squashed commit). Prior review record: architecture PASS (DAG sequencing B1->BF1->BF2->BF3->{B2,B3} confirmed coherent, zero production diff, emitter-mapping dispositions spot-checked), adversarial found one BLOCKING governance finding (AMD-005 §15.1's ratification quotation cited the wrong reviewed-package SHA — pre-fix ce1d0e4688 instead of PASS-reattested 7442bb9060; citation-only, substance always correct) — escalated per STOP conditions, architecture-authorized as non-discretionary record repair (no new maintainer ratification required, governance §10), landed as standalone commit f1b59d2dd. AMD-005 (Framework Compiler Conformance Rescope) itself maintainer-ratified and landed at 34fe8167f (housekeeping squash of the original four-commit landing sequence — content byte-identical, tree unchanged; superseded pre-fix candidate ce1d0e4688/1ff1f83d8e, reviewed package 7442bb9060/69502487b, ratified bundle aa757eecc/0c078357b, original ratification-record commit ade8a301b, preserved on branch backup/pre-amd005-squash). BF2 next legal once this transition is validated. EVIDENCE RE-BINDING (evidence/BF1/BF1-summary.md): original digest unrecoverable (matched no committed artifact); re-bound to this block real landing summary."
docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:297:notes = "REOPEN #4 RESOLVED. Two triggers: (1) BV0-relanding scoping consult Q2/Q4 — named import-specifier order compared positionally (now cosmetic in the normalizer) and script-less SFC bindingMetadata passed truthy-empty instead of undefined (wrong render-arity golden, fixed). (2) Mapping axis was structurally unsound — compared candidate-vs-official source maps despite the project's own Compiled-Output Conformance rule allowing cosmetic generated-byte divergence, so two compilers' maps necessarily describe two different documents. Binding maintainer direction: source-map correctness is judged only against the exact authored SFC. Replaced end to end with a self-referential oracle (new src/mapping-oracle.mjs): map contract/bounds, source identity, per-segment truthfulness via a closed relation table, bidirectional round-trip completeness, fragment-first assembly composition, structural generated-only range detection against fabricated provenance. Four independent review rounds; rounds 1-3 each found and fixed real defects (false doc citation; synthetic-range enforcement that never ran on the real path; non-position-exact relations; an incomplete binding-pattern check; over/under-broad generated-range detection). Round 4 (review-round cap) found two final defects, fixed and independently re-verified by the program orchestrator against committed source rather than a fifth agent round. Disclosed bounded residuals (non-blocking, stated in-module): a reference-occurrence fallback relation not fully position-exact (267/812 corpus occurrences); the boundary check intentionally unenforced on ranges nested inside a larger legitimately-mapped expression; map.file unvalidated (no golden carries it). A related maintainer optimization concern was investigated in parallel (evidence/BF2/reopen4/optimization-vs-conformance-investigation.md) — partially confirmed (narrow waste, e.g. an unused-import case now flagged for BV0), no evidence of deeper architectural cost; disposed as narrow ADOPT-NOW items plus one CLAUDE.md-level DEFER (FC-VUE-002, owned by BV1/BS1). Full detail: evidence/BF2/reopen4/{context-packet,landing-record}.md. No production compiler code, no verter_session, no Svelte file, no crates/verter_vue_conformance/corpus touched — scope confirmed via diff by the program orchestrator. Independently re-verified: harness 411/411, verter_vue_conformance 8/8. BF1 not reopened (unaffected both times). BV0 and BF3 unblocked, next legal once this transition is validated; BV0's own restack still additionally waits on AMD-007/BV0A ratification (docs/arch/refactor/rev11/amendments/AMD-007-assembled-module-source-map-interim.md, PENDING)."
docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:402:notes = "Four findings corrected in their root-cause owners; all four named targets enabled and green. The first row understated the work: the each-block flag is coupled to the item read form, so clearing it while still emitting a signal deref produces a module that mounts and renders WRONG - non-reactive items are now demoted to a distinct kind. The fourth was corrected in the shared framework-surface leg, NOT the projector the charter names; a grok pass proved that leg has three consumers and a projector fix would have forked the shared surface - charter wording inaccurate, recorded not edited. While extending the gate outcome enum the block found the gate NEVER COMPARED the oracle verdict, so a state asserting failure could silently record a passing cell; the verdict is now compared and the empty-divergence state is structurally unrepresentable. Both seats found real defects, two of them regressions this block introduced. Seven out-of-scope defects deferred as ignored characterizations proven RED with named owners, including a pre-existing non-ASCII identifier panic. Gate PASS on the exact landing tree (24413/24413, 3 suites clean, 8634/8634); a first run FAILED on 4 tests proven to be concurrent-gate contention by isolated re-runs, not assumed. Detail: evidence/BS0/landing-record.md."
docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:444:notes = "COMPLETE - all three rows executed. The batch route now selects each input carrier from its own canonical id, derived at one function that takes NO language argument so a call site has nothing to get wrong. Deriving it was insufficient: the adversarial seat caught that the skip predicate compared BYTES only, so a canonical previously registered under another carrier kept it for the whole batch and the derived language never reached the host; the predicate now consumes the built registration and the intermediate raw collection is gone, so the decision structurally cannot see fewer fields than the registration carries. Earlier pass: one absent-response contract for a missing virtual node confined to a shared classifier, and the non-Vite bundler product carrying the host map. Gate PASS on all three surfaces (24417/24417, 8638/8638). ONE PUBLIC-CONTRACT NARROWING RATIFIED by direct maintainer act: an id naming no carrier is no longer compiled into a component module. Two deferrals with owners recorded. Detail: evidence/BRT0/landing-record.md."
docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:465:notes = "Parse recovery diagnostics and stable identities. The prior BLOCKING conformance verdict is genuinely resolved, not re-labelled. Two process defects were corrected first: a conformance seat had been run by an off-roster tool on the FALSE premise that the rostered tool was down - a direct probe showed it healthy and the invocation faulty - and the committed parse-facet evidence recorded rows as passing with diagnostics the tree could not emit at that level, which is false evidence rather than stale. Re-running the rostered seat against the landed tree found the off-roster leads credible but incomplete AND new defects on each subsequent fix, requiring four further fix rounds each independently re-reviewed by a rostered seat plus a separate empirical agent that re-ran oracle-backed regenerations rather than trusting a round self-report. Round 5 caught a critical fail-closed regression that had reintroduced an already-fixed IDE-breaking bug class. Round 7 was caught ONLY by the full canonical gate - targeted crate suites across three prior rounds all missed a real regression in a pre-existing integration test one layer removed from the edits; the gate re-ran clean afterwards on all three surfaces and is the authoritative verification. Architecture and adversarial PASS carry forward unchanged from the original round-3 verdicts because rounds 4-7 never touched the structural-sealing redesign those mandates evaluated. Evidence regeneration confirmed byte-identical. Two items dispositioned as pre-existing and out of scope: a trybuild fixture failing identically at base and tip with zero diff in range, and a narrow CSS diagnostic-code fidelity gap (CSS work suspended program-wide). Detail: evidence/B2/landing-record.md."

docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-u2-reducers.md:330:- `relation_negative_and_unknown_paths_are_fast` — the PART 1 §6.2 perf-hardening guard for the hottest reducer: the common not-assignable / no-match / unknown outcome is decided by cheap structural discriminators (primitive / literal / shape-tag / brand-identity / arity mismatch) BEFORE opening the coinductive-SCC scope or relating members pairwise, and a repeat negative is served from the full-`Relate`-identity pair memo (§6) — both WITHOUT entering the SCC / member-recursion machinery and without allocating a relation proof, a fact payload, or a session transaction; memo locality (interned-ID keys, contiguous per-relation-root assumption scope) is benched. docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-cache-export-session.md:506:Context: The published projection is the closed `GraphTypeNode` type-value projection of every U2 type value, plus the TS `TypeDescriptor` projection (`@verter/type-ir` + `@verter/component-meta`) that consumes the wire payload STRUCTURALLY — driving every semantic decision from the typed IR, never from raw / display strings (the Typed-IR-Only Resolver Rule, the Component-Meta Native vs Compat Rule). docs/arch/parselower-design.md:12:This v3 keeps the endorsed staged skeleton and bakes in the 7 review refinements (the v1→v2→v3 review chain endorsed the direction; v3 finalizes the stage-1/2/3 foundation). The breaking phase was re-sequenced per the architecture ruling at the orchestration ledger (the former monolithic "Stage 3C / Stage 5 atomic macro-producer" framing split into Stage 5A + Stage 6-prep + a reordered Stage 6), and then re-sequenced AGAIN per the architecture tie-breaker ruling at the orchestration ledger (Ruling 1 + Ruling 2 / defer-all-5A under (iii), adopted by the CTO as R1) — Stage 5A was DEFERRED behind a NEW non-breaking consumer-readiness prerequisite, **Stage 5A-prep**, so that the full macro-arg producer cutover (all four sites) could land atomically only once that prerequisite was satisfied. That prerequisite was SATISFIED and Stage 5A then LANDED: Stages 1-4 are NON-BREAKING (additive / dual-read; LANDED), the **Stage 5A-prep** prerequisite is LANDED (NON-BREAKING; refactor commit `8ff601882`), and **Stage 5A** — the atomic four-site macro hot-mirror structural producer cutover — is LANDED on the resume branch (`mom/stage5a-resume`): the session macro hot mirror is the SOLE production producer of the macro type-argument structural carriers and all four macro-arg sites read it (carriers flow through production). The inserted **Stage 6-prep** (NON-BREAKING — graph-native `whole_env()` consumer readiness; FOUR codex-confirmed-exhaustive consumers each gain a bounded graph-native reader beside the retained whole-env oracle) is LANDED on the resume branch (`mom/stage6prep`). **Stage 6 — the bounded Option-B declaration-body handle-payload / hot-read cutover (mint `HotTypeRef` in the `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor over the `Instantiate` result the graph-bearing dispatch producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer; the migrated graph-backed semantic readers go handle-native and the superseded bundle-stored hot prepared layer (`HotPrepared*`) is DELETED — handles mint on demand at `decl_body_hot_ref`; `DeclBodyMemo` + the lower-crate `Prepared*` are fact+locator `NoTypeExpr` (the LIVE end-state — TWO memoized pockets excepted: `LoweredTypeDecl.type_parameters: Vec<TypeParam>` retains constraint/default `Arc<TypeExpr>` (`decl_body_memo.rs:104`), feeding locator/binder lowering (`locator_deref.rs:363`) and the external frontier (`external_type_frontier.rs:152`); docs/arch/parselower-design.md:61:- HANDLED today, split by HOW the args are reached: (a) EMISSION / CONSTRUCTION — the query-free structural lowerer CONSTRUCTS the three carriers via the `new_typeof`/`new_bare_ref`/`new_import_type` constructors (passing `type_args` IN; construction is not a descent tail) (and its pre-lowering extends-infer collector reaches the mapped `as`-remap `name_type` while walking the input `TypeExpr`); (b) ACCESSOR-READING SCAN/CLASSIFY walkers — the absorb infer-scan, the open-node value-body / enumeration-domain walk, AND the `subtree_references` reachability scan (the `build_mapped_type` key-independence hoist) DESCEND carrier args through the shared `SemanticNodeData::carrier_type_args` accessor; (c) the reconstruction / render / identity BOUNDARIES — split by whether they REBUILD: raise/materialize and display READ head fields through the `typeof_head`/`bare_ref_head`/`import_type_head` accessors and descend args through `SemanticNodeData::carrier_type_args` to materialize / render (NO rebuild); the substitute re-intern arm ALONE rebuilds the carrier node via `SemanticNodeData::map_carrier_type_args` (after descending args via `carrier_type_args`), while the structural `eq`/`hash` compare/hash the opaque carrier payload (derived on the carrier struct). docs/arch/parselower-design.md:204:Producer-activation guard sequence (per the decider ruling): the dormant zero-caller guard `structural_lowerer_has_no_production_caller_until_carrier_resolution` was REMOVED at **Stage 5A** (LANDED). The producer is now COLLAPSED into ONE private module: `lower_type_expr_structural` (and the two other producer-capable builders `build_macro_hot_ref` / `build_script_setup_seed_frames`) are BARE module-private `fn`s (NO visibility modifier) in `structural_carrier_producer::macro_arg_producer`, reachable from outside only through the `pub(crate)` `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` accessor. The single-producer guarantee has TWO REGIMES: the FOREIGN case is COMPILER-CONFINED (no module outside `macro_arg_producer` can NAME the private builders — a compile error, E0603 / E0433 — so a second producer in a foreign module is unrepresentable by construction); the SAME-MODULE case is NOT compiler-confined (Rust privacy is module-scoped, so a second producer written INSIDE `macro_arg_producer.rs` CAN name the builders) and is instead POLICED by the bounded single-producer architecture guards. The tripwires are (a) the privacy-shape guard `structural_carrier_producer_lowerer_is_module_private` (asserts all three builders stay bare module-private `fn`s, single-defined, not re-exported), (b) the ordering tripwire `no_production_macro_arg_eager_lowering_outside_mirror` (bans eager macro-arg lowering outside the mirror), (c) the purity guard `macro_hot_mirror_producer_is_pure_no_route_resolution` (the mirror does no host route lookup), and (d) the entry-surface guard `macro_hot_mirror_exposes_single_crate_visible_producer_entry` — a BOUNDED defense-in-depth tripwire (NOT an exhaustive proof) that polices the same-module residual. Guard (d) pins `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` as the sole crate-visible producer entry across the realistic outward API surface `pub` / `pub(crate)` / `pub(in crate)` (the exact crate-root restricted path — `pub(in crate)` is identical crate-wide visibility to `pub(crate)`), covering module-level FREE functions AND associated functions inside INHERENT `impl` blocks, plus the VALUE-exposure surface (a crate-visible `const`/`static`/inherent-assoc-const binding a builder as an fn-pointer value), the TRAIT-exposure surface (only the hand-written `Debug`/`Clone` impls for `MacroHotMirror` — bare or std-spelled — are allowed; any other trait impl, a trait def/alias, or an allowlisted impl whose method/assoc-const reaches a builder is rejected), and the EXACT `mod.rs` re-export shape (a PRIVATE `mod macro_arg_producer;` carrying no attribute other than a strict `#[cfg(test)]`, plus exactly `pub(crate) use macro_arg_producer::{macro_type_arg_hot_ref, MacroHotMirror};` — no alias/glob/extra leaf/`pub`-widened decl/`#[path]` re-root). Item test-gating is classified by cfg SATISFIABILITY/ENTAILMENT (`#[cfg(any(test, debug_assertions))]` / `#[cfg(any(feature = "x", test))]` / `#[cfg(not(test))]` are PRODUCTION-satisfiable and COUNTED; only a predicate that ENTAILS test is excluded) and `#[cfg_attr(...)]` is NOT an item gate (it conditionally applies an attribute and never removes the item, so a `#[cfg_attr(test, …)] pub(crate) fn` producer is COUNTED). The PRIMARY by-construction protection remains the module-privacy of the lowerer itself — no outside module can name `lower_type_expr_structural`, so a second OUTWARD producer is unrepresentable without wrapping it; guard (d) is the layered secondary tripwire over the same-module residual. The KNOWN RESIDUAL gaps a `syn` scan cannot SOUNDLY close are the macro-expanded / out-of-tree shapes: a foreign-fn `extern` block, a `#[path = "…"]` module rooted OUTSIDE `crates/verter_session/src/**`, and macro-expanded / build-substituted / out-of-tree proc-macro producers — the IRREDUCIBLE residual is trust in the one sanctioned producer plus compiler bugs / build substitution. (The earlier codex-deferred P1 hardening row — `cfg_attr` item suppression, production-satisfiable feature cfgs, and trait-dispatch exposure — is now CLOSED by the strengthened guard (d): cfg_attr is correctly never an item gate, feature cfgs are satisfiability-classified, and trait/value exposure is covered.) The enum-wide anti-tail structural guard `no_named_type_args_field_outside_opaque_carrier` is **PRE-EXISTING (pre-Stage-6)** (registered in `critical_rules_have_guards.rs`, implemented in `carrier_encapsulation_guards.rs`) — present before the Stage-6 work and ORTHOGONAL to it. Stage 6 Option B did NOT widen the structural-lowerer privacy guard: the Option-B flip MINTS handles in the `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor over the `Instantiate` result the graph-bearing dispatch producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer, and does NOT route declaration bodies through the query-free structural lowerer, so `lower_type_expr_structural` stays a bare module-private `fn` with the macro hot mirror its SOLE production caller and its privacy-shape guard UN-widened. A future query-free decl-body structural-template producer, if ever pursued, is a separate design with its own guarded surface — not this flip.
docs/arch/parselower-design.md:215:FINAL STATE: the Stage-8 transitional materialize allowlist reached 0 (LANDED); residual Stage-4 dual-read is read-compat only (both arms route through the SAME dispatch — not a second resolution engine), faithful to CLAUDE.md's "one clean cutover / no double branches". The **Stage-5A** macro hot-mirror producer is likewise NOT a permanent dual path (authority: the decider ruling): it is a SINGLE-ENTRY producer — the macro hot mirror is the one production caller of `lower_type_expr_structural` (the eager `lower.rs` declaration-body path is unchanged — the LANDED Stage 6 Option-B flip mints `HotTypeRef` handles in the `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor over the `Instantiate` result the graph-bearing dispatch producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer, and does NOT route declaration bodies through the structural lowerer), every macro call site reads that ONE mirror, and carrier resolution re-enters the ONE dispatch. It is not a callsite-scattered structural-vs-eager selection (which WOULD be a forbidden permanent dual lowering policy); the single entry is enforced by the COLLAPSED private module (`lower_type_expr_structural` is a bare module-private `fn` — NO visibility modifier — in `structural_carrier_producer::macro_arg_producer`, reachable from outside only through the `pub(crate)` `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` accessor: the FOREIGN case is compiler-confined and the SAME-MODULE residual is policed by the strengthened single-producer guards, pinned by the privacy-shape guard). Stage 6 Option B landed; the macro hot mirror remains the SOLE production caller of `lower_type_expr_structural`, and the single-entry guarantee + its privacy guard are unchanged by it (Option B mints handles in `decl_body_hot_ref` over the `Instantiate` result the graph-bearing dispatch producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer, not through the structural lowerer). A decl-body structural-lowerer flip, if ever pursued, is separate future work with its own guarded surface. Per the architecture tie-breaker ruling at the orchestration ledger (R1), Stage 5A was DEFERRED behind the non-breaking `Stage 5A-prep` mapped-key-domain consumer-side carrier resolution precisely BECAUSE the partial interim — sites 1/2/4 read the mirror while `vue_exec` (site 3) stays eager — would have been a second base producer for the same macro type-argument syntax (the forbidden dual path), and a mapped-only deferral would silently lose slots (`slot_fields()` → `[]`). Now that `Stage 5A-prep` has LANDED (refactor commit `8ff601882`) AND Stage 5A itself has LANDED as the atomic all-four-sites flip (every macro call site reads the ONE mirror, single-entry, carrier resolution re-enters the ONE dispatch), the end-state is in force: NOT a dual path. The block 8-A4 Kind-B raise-then-decide conversion has LANDED (the interim bridge is gone — the raise-then-decide callers C1-C4 now decide on the node-domain facts/key and materialise once at a registered sink, so no Kind-B dual PATH remains; C5, the route fixpoint, is converted to the node-domain interned-shape cursor — the sealed `AdmittedRouteProjectionNode` compared by interned `RaisedShapeKey`, ONE resolver, NOT a second resolution path, so it is not a dual path either); the transitional materialize allowlist reached 0 and the hot-materialize fence `hot_path_never_calls_materialize_type_expr` is green at zero offenders (the global Unknown-as-control-flow fence it shipped alongside has since been deleted — the typed-degradation cutover removed the sentinel control-flow shape it scanned for), leaving ZERO permanent dual path. Stated explicitly so a reviewer does not read the transitional dual-read or the Stage-5A single-entry producer as a rule violation.
docs/arch/parselower-design.md:218:Stage 6 (the bounded Option-B declaration-body handle-payload / hot-read cutover) was the top regression risk — exhaustive `whole_env()` enumeration was mandatory, which is exactly why Stage 6-prep (the non-breaking graph-native `whole_env()` consumer replacements) preceded it. The ratified Stage-6 mechanism is **Option B** (mint `HotTypeRef` in the `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor over the `Instantiate` result the graph-bearing dispatch producer drives via the RESOLVING lowerer; the migrated graph-backed semantic readers carry handles minted on demand at `decl_body_hot_ref` (the superseded bundle-stored hot prepared layer `HotPrepared*` is DELETED); `DeclBodyMemo` + the lower-crate `Prepared*` are fact+locator `NoTypeExpr` — two memoized pockets excepted: `LoweredTypeDecl.type_parameters: Vec<TypeParam>` retains constraint/default `Arc<TypeExpr>` (`decl_body_memo.rs:104`), feeding locator/binder lowering (`locator_deref.rs:363`) and the external frontier (`external_type_frontier.rs:152`); and `TypeParamBinding.constraint/default` keeps `Arc<TypeExpr>` bounds in cached prepared decl bundles, owned by the type-parameter-bound confinement block), NOT a "global structural producer flip" routing declaration bodies through the query-free structural lowerer — that is a separate, deferred, future query-free design. The macro hot-mirror producer (Stage 5A, LANDED — the atomic four-site producer cutover, on top of the now-LANDED non-breaking `Stage 5A-prep` mapped-key-domain consumer-side carrier resolution at `8ff601882`) is done; Stage 8's compat materialization fence LANDED (transitional allowlist 0; reverse boundary is the sealed `OutputProjector`, not an open compat bridge). De-risked by: non-breaking Stages 1-4 (carriers + demand resolution + handle-capable consumers all landed before any producer flip), the LANDED non-breaking `Stage 5A-prep` mapped-key-domain consumer-readiness gate (which unblocked the `defineSlots<mapped>` / structural-`BareRef` mapped-source path so the macro producer cutover could land atomically), then the now-LANDED narrow single-entry macro producer at Stage 5A (no declaration-body lowering, all four macro-arg sites read the mirror atomically), then the now-LANDED non-breaking Stage 6-prep graph-native consumer readiness gate (four codex-confirmed-exhaustive `whole_env()` consumers each with a bounded graph-native reader beside the retained oracle), then the now-LANDED Stage 6 Option-B declaration-body handle-payload / hot-read flip (the macro hot mirror remains the SOLE production caller of `lower_type_expr_structural`). Stages 7-9 (cache/artifact cutover, compat materialization fence, transitional-bridge deletion) have LANDED — the hot-materialize fence is enabled and green at zero offenders; the typed-degradation end-state has since LANDED (the global Unknown fence and its deferral doc are deleted), and the residual-reader final state is recorded in `docs/arch/authored-shape-graph-native-migration-deferral.md`.
docs/arch/parselower-design.md:224:- **LANDED in 8-A3 (the durable Kind-A fence).** Block 8-A3 landed the durable reverse-materialization (`SemanticNodeId → TypeExpr`) OUTPUT fence for the TRUE OUTPUT SINKS (Kind A) as a SEALED-TRAIT CAPABILITY — **`OutputProjector`** + the sealed carriers **`OutputTypeExpr`** (plain-raise) / **`MaterializedOutputTypeExpr`** (reduce-then-raise) — in `project_semantic_dispatch/output_materialization.rs`. The callable boundary MOVED OFF `ProjectSemanticDispatch` onto the `OutputProjector` capability; the carrier payload is a PRIVATE inner `TypeExpr` whose only reader is a capability-gated accessor (`into_type_expr` / `type_expr`, each taking `&impl OutputProjector`); each true output-**SINK** module (the exact module that projects — `meta_resolve::projectors::output_sink` (a DEDICATED terminal sink submodule, re-exported at `meta_resolve::projectors::MetaResolveProjectorsOutputCap` — extracted EXACTLY so the parent `projectors`' non-sink helpers (`macro_payload_substrate`, `published_reducer`, the per-kind projector children) cannot mint), `meta_resolve::materialize::field_types`, `host_manage::component_meta_methods`, `typeinfo::raise`, `typeinfo::framework_surface::{vue_exec,svelte_exec}` (`vue_exec`'s whole reachable scope — `vue_exec` + its `normalize` child — is output-only, so the single cap is correct), `component_meta_query_engine::{registry_decl,surface}` — **EIGHT per-sink caps**) owns a private-field capability whose constructor is `pub(in <sink-module>)` — scoped to the SINK, NOT the subtree. `pub(in P)` grants the mint to `P` AND every module at-or-under `P`, so the mint scope is scoped to a TERMINAL output sink whose entire reachable production module tree is itself output-only — that (not "per-leaf") is what makes the fence compiler-enforced for in-subtree code: a Kind-B bridge sibling (`meta_resolve::dispatch_helpers`, `host_manage::eval_env`) — or a non-sink helper sibling — is NOT reachable from any sink's mint scope and cannot name any cap's constructor (a planted `*OutputCap::new` there is `E0624`). In safe production Rust OUTSIDE the audited output-materialization payload vault, `OutputTypeExpr` and `MaterializedOutputTypeExpr` do not expose a readable `TypeExpr` field (the inner `TypeExpr` lives in the deeply-private `carrier::payload` vault): capability-free unwrap is unrepresentable by field access, auto-deref, arbitrary trait impls, or inherent methods, and the only production APIs returning `TypeExpr` / `&TypeExpr` are the capability-gated `into_type_expr` / `type_expr` accessors. The seal is COMPILER-enforced both OUT of crate and WITHIN it: `mod sealed` is PRIVATE (not `pub(super)`) inside `mod projector`, so `projector::sealed::Sealed` is nameable ONLY from within `projector` — a sibling `carrier` / `carrier::payload` (or any other crate module) that writes `impl projector::sealed::Sealed for HotCap` is `E0603` (module `sealed` is private), so the sealed trait cannot be implemented for a non-sanctioned type even from a sibling owner-descendant scope; the `output_projector_owner_registration_inventory` topology guard is the defense-in-depth backstop, not the primary. The mint half is the same shape (COMPILER-ENFORCED as the PRIMARY barrier): a hot / session / Kind-B mint is `E0624` / `E0451` (the terminal-sink capability constructor is unreachable from any non-sink module), a hot carrier-unwrap is `E0277` (unsatisfied `OutputProjector` bound — the trait is sealed) AND the inner `TypeExpr` is not even a readable field, and a hot `.type_expr_for_test()` is `E0599` (the carrier `_for_test` accessors are gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` — the production-unreachable test-support feature activated only by `verter_session`'s own dev-dep self-edge — so they are COMPILE-ABSENT from every production build, unlike a `debug_assertions` gate which would be present in ordinary debug builds). The residual TRUSTED surface is the inline payload vault + the projector registration module (and the by-name identity of which owner types are sinks), whose exact item/module/signature shape is structurally guarded as DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH (a CLOSED structural allowlist, NOT the primary barrier); this claim does NOT cover guard deletion, deliberate edits inside that trusted vault, or unsafe code unless the crate forbids unsafe globally. The FFI boundary became the session-owned BYTES facade `VerterHost::project_node_to_type_expr_json_bytes` (mints the capability + materializes + unwraps + serializes to wire JSON internally; NAPI wraps the bytes in a `Buffer`, WASM does `String::from_utf8` — schema byte-identical, functionally identical); the old `pub fn project_node_to_type_expr` and the all-`pub`-field `MaterializedTypeExpr` struct are DELETED. The raw `raise_node_to_type_expr` primitive STAYS module-private; the reduce-then-raise orchestrator `raise_and_reduce_with_context` STAYS `pub(super)`; the shell output seam `output_shell_raise_sealed` returns a SEALED `Option<OutputTypeExpr>` (never a bare `TypeExpr`) so a `project_semantic_dispatch` sibling reaching the `pub(super)` seam cannot launder. The fence SHAPE is pinned by mechanism-matched guards over that trusted surface (a CLOSED structural allowlist, complete-by-construction): the EXACT module topology of the owner file — inline `projector` / `projector::sealed` / `carrier` / `carrier::payload` and nothing else, with item/impl/trait-position macro invocations, `include!`, unknown attributes, a `sealed::Sealed` alias `use`, and any owner-file `TypeExpr` alias BANNED — plus the sanctioned sink set (the explicit `impl OutputProjector` / `impl sealed::Sealed` self-types, compared by FULL self-type path as a MULTISET so a duplicate / last-ident-colliding registration is caught) by `output_projector_owner_registration_inventory`; a closed item/signature allowlist over the carrier/payload vault (every fn returning `TypeExpr` must be capability-gated or exactly test-gated) by `output_carriers_have_no_inherent_typeexpr_escape_method`; every carrier/payload struct field private regardless of spelled type by `output_carrier_payload_fields_are_private`; an accidental-regression CANARY for the common `Deref` / `AsRef` / `Borrow` trait escapes (NOT proof-complete — completeness for the unbounded escape-trait surface comes from the payload vault) in `project_semantic_dispatch/output_materialization_guards.rs`; the out-of-crate visibility boundary by the trybuild `output_projector_non_owner_impl_is_compiler_sealed`; the mintable `TestOutputCap` staying `#[cfg(test)]`-gated by `test_output_cap_not_visible_or_mintable_in_non_test_builds`; the terminal-sink mint scope by `output_cap_mint_scope_is_per_leaf_not_subtree` — a Rust-VISIBILITY reachable-module-tree model: for every `mint: pub(in P)` it builds the production module tree at P-and-below (excluding `#[cfg(test)]` modules) and default-DENIES any reachable module not on the cap's exact sink-module allowlist (a new non-sink descendant fails WITHOUT a denylist entry), paired with the walker self-test `mint_scope_module_tree_walker_self_test_discriminates`; the carrier `_for_test` gate by `carrier_for_test_accessors_are_test_support_gated_not_debug_assertions`; the sealed raise seam by `raise_output_seam_returns_sealed_carrier_not_bare_type_expr` (recursing non-test modules + transitive `TypeExpr` aliases) — STRENGTHENED at 8-A4 to assert ZERO public/restricted `raise.rs` bare-`TypeExpr` fns, no sanctioned bridge exception remaining.
docs/arch/parselower-design.md:226:- **`RaisedShapeKey` is now an INTERNED STRUCTURAL term, not a `TypeExpr` wrapper.** It is a `u32` intern id carrying a prehash + structural eq (no longer the old `TypeExpr`-wrapping key whose derived `PartialEq` was the comparison). `RaisedShapeFacts` (`materialized` / `expanded_surface` / `can_shell_raise`) are computed BOTTOM-UP by `RaisedShapeAlg` with NO `TypeExpr` allocation — the facts are read straight off the graph nodes, not off a built `TypeExpr`.
docs/arch/parselower-design.md:227:- **The Kind-B raise-then-decide callers (C1-C4) decide node-domain and materialise once at a registered sink; C5 (the route fixpoint) is converted to the node-domain interned-shape cursor.** C1 (`execute_to_type_expr`, DELETED) → the demand-bound surface adapters in `resolver_core::component_meta_query_engine::surface`; C2 (`project_slot_binding_member_with_terminal_id`) is now node-only; C3 (`instantiate_local_generic_ref_via_dispatch`) → `instantiate_local_generic_ref_published`; C4 (the `eval_env` defineModel / ProjectPath / slot-binding raises) → the sink-owned demand methods `expand_define_model_output` / `expand_generic_project_path_output` / `expand_slot_binding_output` in `host_manage::component_meta_methods` (the eval_env branches pass only the closed demand — resolver ctx + owner canonical + macro index + the per-branch terminal demand — never a raw `SemanticNodeId`; the demand method resolves the carrier head + terminal INTERNALLY and materialises the produced node at the module-private sealed sink — the module-private `AdmittedExpansionNode` + `materialize_admitted_expansion_node`). C5 (the route fixpoint) stabilises on interned `shape_engine::RaisedShapeKey` identity via the sealed `AdmittedRouteProjectionNode` carrier across all its adapter legs and materialises EXACTLY ONCE at the registered terminal surface sink (`materialize_route_projection_node`) — no per-iteration materialisation remains, and the fence `hot_path_never_calls_materialize_type_expr` is enabled and green at zero offenders.

docs/arch/native-flow-return.md:508:- `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs` — the `FunctionFlowGraph` producer: builds the sparse per-function dependence graph ONCE from `FunctionBodySkeleton` with the typed edge classes (`value-def`, `path-write`, `eval-effect`, `narrowing-predicate`, `control-region`, `closure-escape`, `loop-summary`, `try/finally-override` — the `FlowEdgeKind` enum) over interned slots / paths / regions. Built once per function per content version from the retained snapshot — eagerly or lazily per the share-vs-split checks — never rebuilt per query or demand. **No type lowering at build time** — it is a structural skeleton; types along an edge resolve on demand only when a slice traverses them. Fully arena-detached (`Send + Sync + 'static`). This block lands the graph + the value-def / path-write / eval-effect / control-region edge classes; the narrowing-predicate edges land across the `U6.NARROW_*` narrowing sub-blocks (collectively — one shared `FlowFrame` lattice) and the closure-escape / loop-summary / try/finally-override edges in U6.LOOP_CLOSURE (each ADDS its edge class to this same graph, never a second structure).
docs/arch/native-flow-return.md:515:- `crates/verter_session/src/flow_return/result.rs` + `error.rs` — DEFINE the two U6-extension result types per the locked design's split result/carrier contract (C1): the SUCCESS carrier `FlowReturnResult { return_type, can_fall_through, degradation: Option<FlowReturnDegradation> }` (the `ReadSetSignature`, actual `satisfied_projection`, self roots, and publication metadata ride the published-value carrier — `MemoEntry` / `PublishedMemoCandidate` — never the domain result; a refusal carries its typed `NonAdmissionReason`) and `ResolvedCallResult` (the call-resolution result value the `ResolveCall` arm carries — consumed by U6.CALL_RESOLVE's `build_resolve_call`); `FlowReturnError` (the typed `Err` arm of `AuditedResult`, carrying the `FlowReturnFailure`-class no-value outcomes).
docs/arch/native-flow-return.md:518:- `crates/verter_session/src/cache_runtime/` — register `FlowSliceHashNode` (content-addressed: key carries the per-function **`flow_body_stable_hash`** — the body-sensitive / cosmetic-insensitive hash over `FunctionBodySkeleton` + `FunctionFlowGraph`, NOT `parse_stable_hash`, so `return { b: 1 }` and `return { b: 2 }` key distinct slices — plus `parse_env_hash` + `parser_version` + `function_part` + the `ReturnProjectionDemand` slice identity) and `FlowSliceLoweredBodyNode` (keyed additionally on the slice hash) as `ArtifactNode` impls — memory-side registration on the existing `ArtifactNode` runtime lands HERE; their PERSISTENT registration is the zero-row owed item `U6.FLOW_SLICE_PERSISTENCE` (← U4); `flow_body_stable_hash` is produced once per function content version by the authoritative structural flow-body producer, alongside the `FunctionFlowGraph` (eager-or-lazy timing and storage placement settled by the share-vs-split checks); the lowered-slice node's eviction follows the standard `remove_canonical(canonical_id)` cascade.
docs/arch/native-flow-return.md:555:- `flow_graph_build_is_shallow_interned_no_lowering` — the PART 1 §6.2 perf-hardening guard for the build path: the `FunctionFlowGraph` build uses compact interned IDs (no owned strings / boxed AST pointers as node/edge/slot/path handles) and lowers NO type at build time (asserts inventory/graph construction produces no `TypeExpr` lowering, `Relate` / `Instantiate` or other resolution dispatch, route lookup, or imported-fact production — those happen only when a slice traverses an edge). It does NOT constrain build timing or region-materialization strategy: eager full structural construction and lazy once-per-content-version construction are BOTH conforming — the locked design's five share-vs-split storage checks (each with its own discriminating executable guard, results recorded per SCC-10; U0 registers them) settle timing and placement at implementation, and a per-query / per-demand rebuild is rejected by `function_flow_graph_built_once_per_function_skeleton`, not here. Discriminating fixture: a large function body with a tiny demand slice (`ReturnType<typeof big>["b"]`) lowers no type and charges no resolution dispatch / route lookup / imported-fact production during graph construction; fails if the build lowers types or produces such facts. Lands HERE with the `FunctionFlowGraph` build.

Each row's declared proof is consumed by its §10.3 proof-consumption rail (PART 2 §10.3; landed shape: the registry-bound driver-calling row body). The discriminating property: the substrate widens a literal return to its primitive (BL01-class) while preserving `as const` (BL09-class), and `ReturnType<typeof myType>['b']` loads only `b`.

docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md:43:| **GI-21** | self-declared test universe (in-binary suite census) | `crates/verter_session/src/framework/mod.rs` holds the four `#[cfg(test)] mod` declarations that constitute one evidence suite's registration set, and `crates/verter_session/src/framework/suite_census.rs` is the IN-BINARY check that each documented `cargo test … <substring>` invocation selects a suite that exists rather than reporting `running 0 tests` / `test result: ok` / exit 0. Each census row is now bound to its suite by a COMPILER-derived identity — `std::any::type_name` of the witness `#[test]` function ITEM the census names, measured as `verter_session::framework::<suite>::this_suite_is_registered_with_the_census` — so removing any ONE of the four `mod` declarations is `error[E0433]`, and a cross-module anchor OUTSIDE the set (`framework::script_facts`'s test module, consuming `suite_census::counts_tests_in`) makes removing ALL FOUR a build error as well. Both directions measured, plants applied and restored: with the anchor, `error[E0433]: cannot find suite_census in framework` at `script_facts_tests.rs:32`; without it, a clean compile and a vacuous `running 0 tests` → `ok` → exit 0. **What that does NOT close.** The census can only observe the universe the binary it runs inside was given: it cannot see a test target the runner never invoked, a `#[cfg]`-gated module the invocation never compiled, or a suite added with no census row at all — its registration set is still four hand-written `mod` lines in one file. Two narrower residues are recorded in `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/BF3/test-invocations.md`: a retarget made INSIDE `suite_census.rs` still passes (measured — the registry decoy plus the repointed row reports `running 1 test` → ok), and the transport row is compiled out entirely without its cargo feature. Scanning is NOT the fix: a landed guard that diffs `mod` lines against `--list` would be exactly the name-keyed source-tree scanner `CLAUDE.md` → "Landed guards are structural, never name-keyed file scanners" forbids. | **OWNER: GI-3** (`gate_contract_integrity`) — this row does not close on its own; it folds into that bar's `independently tree-derived inventory` and `omitted or unowned test` asks. Concretely owed: an inventory derived from the TREE (cargo target discovery plus each target's own libtest `--list`), compared against what the CANONICAL entry point actually executed, so both a suite carrying no census row and a binary the gate never invoked become visible; plus a negative control that removes a whole registration set and is driven through the canonical entry point rather than through the single test binary that would vanish with it. Tests: `gate_contract_integrity::executed_count_matches_tree_derived_inventory` (shared with GI-17), `gate_contract_integrity::removing_a_registration_set_is_detected_by_the_canonical_entry_point`. |
docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md:56:| **GI-8** | banner validator | The canonical fence performs the check mechanically: it extracts the banner region structurally (between the CLI's two `----` rules), requires the region to be CLOSED, matches model and effort WHOLE-LINE, and fails the leg on mismatch — a substituted reviewer is refused, not merely noticed. **An earlier draft of this row claimed a reformatted banner "fails rather than passes"; that was FALSE and the review caught it.** With only the opening rule present, the awk scan ran to EOF, so the whole transcript — prompt echo included — became "the banner region", and the echoed policy lines satisfied both greps while the real banner read `cheap-substituted`. The fence now requires a CLOSED region, requires it to carry the banner's structural keys (`workdir:`/`provider:`/`sandbox:`/`session id:`), and requires exactly one `model:`/`reasoning effort:` line inside it. **It is still not spoof-proof, and the fence says so:** it scrapes a stream that also contains the echoed prompt, so a sufficiently banner-shaped block in the prompt plus a malformed real banner defeats it. Two further attempts to close it by text alone both failed under review — and one of them (anchoring on "the first line is a rule") was factually wrong about the CLI, which prints `Reading prompt from stdin...` and a version line first, so it REJECTED EVERY REAL LEG until it was actually run. That is the row's own justification, twice over: a check whose failure modes are understood only by its author is not a validator, and text-scraping a contaminated stream is the wrong substrate for a gate. What remains missing is CENTRALISED, TESTED enforcement — the check lives in a fence each caller copies rather than in one validated component, so a caller can still omit it, and the delimiter shape is an observed CLI behaviour, not a versioned contract. | One shared validator every leg routes through, with the banner contract pinned. Test SUITE: `banner_mismatch_blocks_the_leg`, `prefix_impostor_model_is_rejected` (a `-sol-mini` must not satisfy `-sol`), `unclosed_banner_region_fails_closed` (the regression above), `slug_in_prompt_echo_does_not_satisfy_the_banner`, `caller_that_skips_the_banner_check_is_rejected`. |

docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:134:Blocked until: U13.PROJECTION done (the adapter reads the published `GraphTypeNode` / TS `TypeDescriptor` projection structurally) and U11.PUBLIC_RELATION_SESSION done (the adapter consumes the public session surface + the request footprint), and the whole U2 + U6 parents done (the macro surfaces it adapts — `defineProps` / `defineEmits` / `defineModel` / `defineSlots` / `withDefaults` payloads and the imported `.vue`-component surfaces — resolve through the U2 reducers and the U6 flow / call solver). This block is the framework-adapter that U15's composite surfaces build on.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:136:Context: The native component-meta payload is the semantic authority and `@verter/component-meta/compat` is a projection layer, not a second semantic pipeline (the Component-Meta Native vs Compat Rule). **The framework-adapter merge landed the Rust framework-surface substrate ahead of order — the `FrameworkAdapterRegistry` (`crates/verter_session/src/framework/registry.rs`) and the Vue/Svelte plan/normalize adapters EXIST in the tree as a true plan/normalize adapter shape (A.15).** This block therefore does NOT build the registry / surface adapter from scratch — it RE-WIRES the merged Rust substrate onto the U11 public session + the U13 published projection, so the framework surface is a STRUCTURAL projection of the engine's published results (the U13 `TypeDescriptor` projection) rather than a per-macro engine; and it BUILDS the still-missing TS thin-adapter layer (`packages/component-meta/src/framework-adapter.ts`, which genuinely does NOT exist) over that re-wired surface. Macro resolution is one shared path, not a per-macro engine (the Macro-Type-Traversal Rule): every macro and every imported `.vue`-component surface resolves through exactly TWO steps — resolve ONE type via the shared typed-IR five-mode dispatch, then normalise per kind (a thin transform, not a resolver); the re-wire MUST NOT rebuild macro meaning (the macro semantics are the shared `ResolveMacroPayload` normalization per unified §3.1.1, which U14 consumes structurally and is forbidden from re-deriving). The single `MacroResolution` row exercises this: `Parameters<NonNullable<T['slot']>>[0]` is a cross-file slot-payload extraction that today stops behind a `semanticMiss` indexed access; lifting it routes the slot-payload type through the shared `IndexedAccess` / `Instantiate` / flow-call reductions (`Parameters<…>` is a U2 intrinsic over the U6-resolved call signature) and normalises the slot binding — NOT a macro-specific walker. The four known Vue mismatch cases (Popover `SlotProps<M>`, theme-alias display, `Button["variants"]["color"]` indexed-access, ContentSearch intersection) are fixed in the NATIVE layer first (fix metadata in the native layer first; Rust owns resolution, declaration routing, and graph construction). This block exists now because the composite end-to-end surfaces (U15) are built on the framework adapter, and the adapter must be a thin structural projection before the composite rows can lift end-to-end.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:139:- `crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/surface.rs` (the `FrameworkSurfacePayload` projection driven by `TypeInfoSurface::build`) — project the engine's published `TypeInfoGraphPayload` (the U13 `GraphTypeNode` type-value surface + the relocated side tables) into the `FrameworkSurfacePayload` carrier that embeds `TypeInfoGraphPayload` (the additive `TypeInfoGraphPayload` carrier U8 added at the next free tag, NOT the retired `FrameworkSurfacePayload.graph = 4` embedding — PART 1 §1.5). The framework surface is a structural projection of the engine's typed results; it does no query-time resolution.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:140:- **RE-WIRE the merged Rust framework-surface substrate.** `crates/verter_session/src/framework/registry.rs` (`FrameworkAdapterRegistry`) + the Vue/Svelte framework-surface adapters ALREADY EXIST in the tree (the framework-adapter merge landed them ahead of order). U14 RE-WIRES — does NOT rebuild — this merged Rust substrate so it consumes the U11 public session (the framework-surface request path) and the U13 published projection (the post-U8 `TypeInfoGraphPayload` / `FrameworkSurfacePayload` structural decode). No new Rust `FrameworkAdapterRegistry` is introduced; the existing one is re-pointed onto the published surfaces.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:142:- `packages/component-meta/src/compat/checker.ts` + `packages/component-meta/src/compat/schema.ts` — keep `compat` a projection wrapper over the native payload for `vue-component-meta` interop: it transforms STRUCTURE but must not recover MEANING; every semantic decision reads `prop.type` (`TypeDescriptor`), `prop.rawType` is display passthrough only, and type-role classification is structural (a type is a prop/emit/model/slot type because a Vue macro consumes it, not because its identifier ends with `"Props"` / `"Emits"` / `"Model"` / `"Slots"`).
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:148:- The NEW TS thin-adapter layer (`packages/component-meta/src/framework-adapter.ts`) built over that re-wired surface, projecting the U13 published `TypeDescriptor` surface structurally into the native component-meta payload; `compat` a projection wrapper that transforms structure only.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:155:- Any compat branch that recovers MEANING from `prop.rawType` / a raw / display string (`looksLike*` / `extract*` / `normalize*` / `split*` / `strip*` / `prefer*` / `shouldPrefer*` / `repairOpaque*`) or any hand-rolled type-text splitter — replaced by reading `prop.type` (`TypeDescriptor`) structurally (the Typed-IR-Only Resolver Rule; the `@verter/component-meta` no-rawtype-reads contract).
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:156:- Any identifier-name-suffix type-role classification (`name.ends_with("Props")` etc.) in the adapter / compat layer — replaced by structural macro-participation classification (`AnalyzedMacro.kind` / `parsed_type_argument` / `type_references`).
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:168:- `component_meta_is_thin_framework_adapter_no_second_resolver` — asserts `@verter/component-meta` is a thin `FrameworkSurfacePayload` adapter with no second resolver / expander (cache-owned type recovery only); the framework surface is a structural projection of the published payload, not a re-resolution path.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:171:Critical-rule guards: this block implements the parent's `(CRITICAL)` Component-Meta Native vs Compat Rule, the Macro-Type-Traversal Rule, and the Typed-IR-Only Resolver Rule (the framework adapter projects the published typed surface structurally; the compat layer recovers no meaning from display strings; macro resolution is one shared path). The thin-adapter + no-rawtype-reads + structural-classification guards are these rules' R6 guards: the `@verter/component-meta` no-rawtype-reads contract (`packages/component-meta/tests/no-rawtype-reads.spec.ts`), the published-surface parity (`crates/verter_audit/tests/published_surface_constants_match_ts_port.rs`), and the architecture-guard list for the typed-IR-only pipeline. This block must not regress them. Any new `(CRITICAL)` framework-adapter rule text added to docs registers its guard here in the same change.
docs/arch/native-typeinfo-parity-adapters-final-lift.md:173:Proof requirement: per-row — the `MacroResolution` row is `Ts7Oracle` (the exact TS judgement of the resolved `Parameters<NonNullable<T['slot']>>[0]` slot-payload type) paired with the structural assertion that the terminal slot-payload resolves through the shared reductions without a `semanticMiss` (`OracleAndGuard`). Consumed by the row's §10.3 proof-consumption rail (PART 2 §10.3; landed shape: the registry-bound driver-calling row body).    149	## 2.2 Compositional compiler products and TypeInfo operations
   150	
   151	Compiler requests are a canonical non-empty collection of typed product requests, not one mutually exclusive level or one global profile bag:
   152	
   153	```rust
   154	enum CompileProductRequest {
   155	    RuntimeClient(RuntimeProductRequest),
   156	    RuntimeServer(RuntimeProductRequest),
   157	    IdeCompanion(IdeProductRequest),
   158	    PublicApi(PublicApiProductRequest),
   159	    Declarations(DeclarationProductRequest),
   160	}
   161	
   162	struct RuntimeProductRequest {
   163	    output_profile: OutputProfileId,
   164	    runtime_source_map: Option<RuntimeMapRequest>,
   165	    provenance: Option<ProvenanceRequest>,
   166	    serialization: Option<SerializationProfileId>,
   167	}
   168	
   169	struct IdeProductRequest {
   170	    output_profile: OutputProfileId,
   171	    // SourceProjectionMap is a required part of this product, not an option.
   172	    diagnostics: Option<PresentationProfileId>,
   173	    serialization: Option<SerializationProfileId>,
   174	}
   175	
   176	enum FrameworkCompileRequest {
   177	    Vue(VueCompileRequest),
   178	    Svelte(SvelteCompileRequest),
   179	}
   180	
   181	pub struct CompileRequest {
   182	    pub products: NonEmptyProductRequests, // canonical by product kind; duplicates rejected
   183	    pub framework: FrameworkCompileRequest,
   184	    pub semantic_profile: Option<TypeScriptSemanticProfileId>,
   185	}
   186	```
   187	
   188	The exact Rust shape may use typed builders or product-specific structs. The invariants are binding:
   189	
   190	- multiple products can be requested together and each product owns the output/terminal profiles that affect it;
   191	- no single global `OutputProfileId`, materialization bitset, presentation profile, or serialization profile is presumed valid for every requested product;
   192	- required product parts, such as an IDE `SourceProjectionMap`, are implicit in that product contract and cannot be disabled;
   193	- optional terminal forms, such as runtime map encoding, rendered diagnostics, provenance, or serialization, are attached only to the product/result they materialize;
   194	- equivalent per-product subrequests share prerequisite stages and artifacts through normalized subplan identities;
   195	- irrelevant profiles are rejected or normalized to absence before identity construction; they do not over-key unrelated stages;
   196	- Vue- and Svelte-specific options are typed before planning;
   197	- unsupported combinations and duplicate product kinds are rejected before expensive work;
   198	- no public `analysisLevel=full` or universal options bag widens work implicitly.
   199

   321	`SerializationProfileId` owns wire/container encoding and field layout. It is absent when serialization is not requested.
   322	
   323	Execution profile—native threaded, native single-thread, or WASM single-thread—is not semantic identity for operations declared portable. Capability differences are declared before execution; they do not silently change the result contract.
   324	
   325	An internal refactor leaves the semantic profile unchanged unless observable semantics change. Verter-specific stricter analysis is separately labeled enrichment.
   326	
   327	## 3.3 Compatibility domains
   328	
   329	Version numbers represent interpretation compatibility, not progress.
   330	
   331	Classify every version-like value:
   332	
   333	1. **No compatibility boundary:** internal in-memory implementation detail. Delete it.
   334	2. **Persistent/precomputed boundary:** retain one typed compatibility domain and monotonic epoch only if older bytes could otherwise be misinterpreted.
   335	3. **External wire/protocol boundary:** retain a named domain, schema/epoch policy, and compatibility tests.
   336	
   337	Rules:
   338	
   339	- `0` is a valid first epoch and never means uninitialized;
   340	- epochs are monotonic within a published domain;
   341	- a clean incompatible replacement may create a new domain/namespace whose first epoch is `0`;
   342	- do not reset an existing published domain merely because the project is pre-1.0;
   343	- one domain has one owner;
   344	- no duplicate counters must remain equal by convention;
   345	- ordinary in-memory DTOs are versionless;
   346	- a build/toolchain fingerprint may invalidate disposable caches without per-subsystem progress counters;
   347	- disposable beta caches may be dropped without converters;
   348	- package semver, external tool versions, source revisions, and provider epochs are separate concepts.
