   628	/// `Arc<dyn WorkspaceRead>`. Mutators (`notify_close`, `notify_upsert`,

     1	//! Workspace dependency-direction authority.
     2	//!
     3	//! Walks `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features` and asserts
     4	//! every layered crate's production closure (normal + build, no dev) never
     5	//! reaches a strictly higher layer, except one equality-pinned exception.
     6	//!
     7	//! Inward chain: identity/span/language/contracts → syntax frontends /
     8	//! DTOs → semantic kernel → compiler → session/engine → adapters.
     9	//! Harnesses sit outside; nothing may depend on them.

    17	// a strictly higher layer is a firewall breach unless explicitly,
    18	// equality-pinned excepted.

   108	/// Recorded upward exception: layer-3 `verter_semantic` /
   109	/// `verter_diagnostics` → `verter_workspace` (layer 5) →
   110	/// `verter_scheduler` (unconditional) and `verter_tsgo_api` (native-only).
   111	/// Equality-pinned, never subset-checked — shrinking or growing the set
   112	/// fails until this map is deliberately updated.
   113	///
   114	/// `cargo metadata` without `--filter-platform` unions every target-gated
   115	/// edge, so both scheduler and tsgo_api appear. Target conditions are
   116	/// pinned by
   117	/// `the_ratified_exception_records_its_target_condition_precisely`.

   505	/// Every workspace member `cargo metadata` reports is accounted for
   506	/// (either layered or explicitly named as non-layered tooling) — so adding
   507	/// a new crate to the workspace without updating this matrix fails loudly
   508	/// instead of silently exempting it from the firewall.
   509	#[test]
   510	fn every_workspace_member_is_accounted_for_in_the_layer_matrix() {
   511	    let metadata = workspace_metadata();
   512	    let workspace_members = metadata["workspace_members"]
   513	        .as_array()
   514	        .expect("workspace_members array");
   515	    let packages = metadata["packages"].as_array().expect("packages array");
   516	    let mut member_names: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
   517	    for member_id in workspace_members {
   518	        let member_id = member_id.as_str().expect("member id is a string");
   519	        let pkg = packages
   520	            .iter()
   521	            .find(|p| p["id"].as_str() == Some(member_id))
   522	            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("workspace member `{member_id}` must have a package entry"));
   523	        member_names.insert(
   524	            pkg["name"]
   525	                .as_str()
   526	                .expect("package name is a string")
   527	                .to_string(),
   528	        );
   529	    }
   530	
   531	    let layers = layer_map();
   532	    let mut unaccounted: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   533	    for name in &member_names {
   534	        if !layers.contains_key(name.as_str())
   535	            && !REPOSITORY_TOOLING_NOT_IN_THE_LAYER_MATRIX.contains(&name.as_str())
   536	        {
   537	            unaccounted.push(name.clone());
   538	        }
   539	    }
   540	    assert!(
   541	        unaccounted.is_empty(),
   542	        "workspace member(s) not accounted for in the layer matrix or the tooling exclusion \
   543	         list: {unaccounted:?} — a new crate must be assigned a layer (or explicitly excluded) \
   544	         before this test can prove anything about it"
   545	    );
   546	}
    74	- generated bytes;
    75	- required `SourceProjectionMap` segments and order;
    76	- optional `RuntimeSourceMapData` segments and encoded bytes;
    77	- deterministic `StableEntityId` values;
    78	- diagnostics and canonical order;

    84	Equality is required across cold/warm, direct/prepared/managed, native threaded/native single-thread, WASM single-thread, and legal task schedules for operations declared portable across those profiles.
    85	
    86	Ephemeral `SessionHandle` values are intentionally excluded from cross-regime equality. They are validated against their owning session/cohort and are never represented as deterministic public entity IDs.
    87	
    88	Reusable computation is hermetic over captured observations. It does not read current time, randomness, process-global mutable options, ambient filesystem state, locale, host path formatting, or untracked environment variables. Missing information becomes an explicit data-observation demand, provider request, or typed outcome.
    89	
    90	## 1.4 Simplicity
    91	
    92	Every service object, trait, cache, lock, queue, actor, version, background task, and cross-crate boundary must prove why a direct function, immutable value, private owner, or request-local calculation is insufficient.
    93	
    94	Preference order:
    95	
    96	```text
    97	pure function
    98	-> borrowed/request-local value
    99	-> immutable value object
   100	-> small private owner
   101	-> reusable query when cross-request reuse or validation is valuable
   102	-> executor task when work is coarse and independent
   103	-> actor when a stateful external protocol/resource requires serialized ownership
   104	```
   105	
   106	A one-implementation public trait is rejected unless it is a real substitution boundary. A new crate is rejected unless it establishes a dependency firewall, stable protocol, or multiple credible consumers.
   107	
   108	## 1.5 Constitutional invariants and evidence-selected tactics
   109	
   110	Revision 11 is the strongest defensible target under current evidence, not a claim of globally proven optimality before implementation. `contracts/architecture-falsification.md` classifies decisions as constitutional invariants, repository/product facts, evidence-selected tactics, or deferred research choices.
   111	
   112	Constitutional rules—such as one semantic authority, honest completeness, direct/managed separation, deterministic products, bounded lifetime, and one-path cutovers—cannot be weakened locally. Repository facts are refreshed against the exact checkout. Private tactics may change when measurements disprove them, provided public semantics, ownership, failure behavior, compatibility, and locked gates remain intact. Deferred research does not enter a candidate through speculative “future proofing.”
   113	
   114	A6 accepts an architecture premise ledger. Falsified premises stop affected work, preserve independently valid work, and trigger refresh, rescope, or ADR amendment according to their class.
   115	
   400	1. **Native threaded:** bounded structured CPU execution and owner-affine workers.
   401	2. **Native single-thread:** identical semantics with inline/local execution and no unnecessary concurrent containers.
   402	3. **WASM single-thread:** local/cooperative execution, non-`Send` stores, and no dependency on blocking condvars or native worker pools.
   403	
   404	Optional future WASM threads form a separate capability and do not redefine the single-thread contract.
   405	
   406	`QueryRuntime` semantics—identity, completeness, validation, cancellation, recursion, and admission—are independent from how a profile schedules work.
   407	
   408	# 5. Input authority and snapshots
   409	
   410	## 5.1 One committed input authority
   411	
   412	The managed system has exactly one authority for committed sources, overlays, project topology, and configuration. `InputStore` is the logical role; Revision 11 does not require inventing a new type when the current registered-source/VFS/`PublishedRoot` machinery already owns the invariant and can be converged in place.
   413	
   414	The required invariant is:
   415	
   416	> A reader observes one coherent source/project/configuration state before a commit or after it, never independently sampled roots from different commits.
   417	
   418	An immutable/persistent root published through a short atomic commit is preferred. Equivalent implementations are allowed only if they preserve coherent capture, ordered document mutation, conditional commit, short writer critical sections, bounded memory, and deterministic snapshot identity.
   419	
   420	No parse, compile, TypeInfo, provider, index, cache validation, or external I/O runs inside the input write critical section.
   421	
   422	Before managed QueryRuntime/cache convergence, the current input/VFS/publication owner is classified and its snapshot/fact API is locked. Query infrastructure must not be built around a transitional or independently sampled source view.
   423	
   424	## 5.2 Ordered document mutation
   425	
   426	For each document:
   427	
   428	- accepted incremental edits are applied in order;
   429	- incarnation and document version are validated;
   430	- edits are never dropped or coalesced before source application;
   431	- derived work may be cancelled/coalesced after commit;
   432	- an invalid range/version gap enters an explicit unsynchronized state;
   433	- a later range is never applied to unproven text.
   434	
   435	## 5.3 Lazy input loading
   436	
   437	Reusable semantic/compiler computation performs no unversioned filesystem, network, package-manager, or process read behind a snapshot. Missing information is resolved by the deterministic state machine in `contracts/input-loading.md`.
   438	
   439	At a high level:
   440	
   441	```text
   442	Attempt(snapshot, accumulated observations, resource budget)
   443	  -> Complete(result)
   444	  -> NeedInputs(normalized LoadSet)
   445	  -> TerminalFailure
   446	```
   447	
   448	For `NeedInputs`:
   449	
   450	1. normalize, sort, and deduplicate the complete discovered set for the attempt;
   451	2. compute `delta = requested - previously_requested`;
   452	3. fail with typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` when `delta` is empty and no observed basis changed;
   453	4. enforce total unique-input, byte, dependency-depth, retry, and churn budgets;
   454	5. load `delta` through same-key I/O flights owned outside the semantic kernel;
   455	6. conditionally commit successful and stable negative observations as one coherent batch when the project/configuration basis is still current;
   456	7. capture a new snapshot and restart the whole semantic attempt;
   457	8. never splice newly loaded data into an in-progress derivation.
   458	
   459	A basis change may justify a retry even with the same symbolic dependency, but it consumes the configured churn/restart budget. Partial load success, stable missing observations, and transient loader failures have distinct typed outcomes.
   460	
   461	`TypeInfoEnvironment` is an immutable/data-only observation view. Public/external environments provide bytes and typed metadata, not authoritative semantic fingerprints: Verter validates key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints at the capture boundary. A caller-supplied digest is a hint unless it was minted by a sealed first-party snapshot authority and carries its validity basis. A direct project session returns `NeedInputs` to its caller; a managed embedding may run the outer load/commit/retry loop. The compiler and semantic kernel remain I/O-free.
   462	
   463	# 6. Parsing, source units, and artifacts
   464	
   465	## 6.1 Shared frontend, parse key, and owner domain
   466	
   467	For each language domain, Verter owns one error-tolerant syntax frontend used by IDE and build:
   468	
   469	- Vue carrier;
   470	- Svelte carrier;
   558	-> admitted managed artifact when measured cross-request reuse is valuable
   559	-> optional persistent artifact only when hermetic eligibility is proven
   560	```
   561	
   562	Correct computation does not imply admission. Return-only results are normal.
   563	
   564	# 7. Direct compiler, plans, and compile projections
   565	
   566	## 7.1 Direct compiler boundary
   567	
   568	The direct compiler is a separate product boundary, not an `Engine` mode. It exposes borrowed-source one-shot compilation, explicit prepared reuse, and staged batch planning/emission. It owns no workspace, committed input store, QueryRuntime, provider lifecycle, durable cache set, audit database, or background scheduler.
   569	
   570	No public `dyn CompileTypeInfo`, open resolver trait, `Engine`, `VerterHost`, provider state, or ambient filesystem handle enters the direct compiler.
   571	
   572	## 7.2 Typed operation plan
   573	
   574	The compiler consumes the final compositional request and derives the smallest acyclic prerequisite closure. A cold request plans once by default. Deliberate replanning is allowed only when benchmark evidence shows it is cheaper in total CPU, allocation, retained memory, and complexity than carrying the first plan.
   575	
   576	Unsupported product combinations fail before expensive work. No projection demands means zero TypeInfo construction/call and zero project read.
   577	
   578	## 7.3 Resumable projection protocol
   579	
   580	Project-aware compilation follows:
   581	
   582	```text
   583	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
   584	```
   585	
   586	Conceptually:
   587	
   588	```rust
   589	let mut prepared = compiler.prepare(source_id, source, parse_options)?;
   590	let plan = prepared.plan(request)?;
   591	
   592	loop {
   593	    match type_info.project(plan.projection_batch())? {
   594	        ProjectionOutcome::Complete(facts) => {
   595	            plan.validate_facts(&facts)?;
   596	            break prepared.emit(plan, facts);
   597	        }
   598	        ProjectionOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set) => {
   599	            return CompileAttempt::NeedInputs {
   600	                prepared,
   601	                plan,
   602	                load_set,
   603	            };
   604	        }
   605	    }
   606	}
   607	```
   608	
   609	The exact Rust API may use separate types/builders. The invariants are binding:
   610	
   611	- `CompileProjectionBatch` is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
   612	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized per-product request to the retained prepared root for anti-replay;
   613	- the plan also contains narrower deterministic `ProjectionPlanToken`, product-subplan tokens, and terminal-subplan tokens, so a terminal-only change does not invalidate unchanged semantic/code artifacts;
   614	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, and completeness—not to unrelated presentation or serialization fields;
   615	- stale, replayed, mismatched, or injected facts are rejected before emission;
   616	- no AST borrow, arena pointer, or unvalidated locator crosses external I/O;
   617	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome, not a generic internal error;
   618	- the outer caller may extend a captured project view and retry under the load-wave/no-progress contract;
   619	- a project/configuration basis change invalidates/replans as specified by the token rather than silently reusing facts.
   620	
   621	One-shot convenience APIs may orchestrate local-only semantics synchronously. Project-capable convenience orchestration must remain explicit about loading and retry; compute itself stays I/O-free.
   622	
   623	## 7.4 Sealed `CompileTypeInfo`
   624	
   625	```rust
   626	pub struct CompileTypeInfo<'env> {
   627	    inner: CompileTypeInfoInner<'env>,
   628	}
   629	```
   630	
   631	All first-party local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes execute one `TypeInfoCore`, one `ModuleResolverCore`, and one profile-parameterized relation/inference implementation. External integrations supply captured data observations, not resolution/type/classification semantics.
   632	
   633	No blanket `Send + Sync` applies. Parallel batches use staged prepare/plan, one TypeInfo owner with internal parallelism or explicit first-party per-worker sessions, and parallel emit when legal.
   634	
   635	Validated precomputed facts are optional and accepted only after domain/profile/toolchain/source/dependency/completeness/integrity/size and anti-replay validation. Callers cannot mint arbitrary resolved facts.
   636	
   637	## 7.5 Closed framework projections
   638	
   639	The compiler discovers exact closed projection demands. Vue runtime macro projection contains only facts runtime generation consumes: prop/model identity, optional/required/default association, ordered broad runtime constructors, `skip_check`/typed degradation, provenance anchor, and exact dependency/profile basis.
   640	
   641	Projection follows imports, aliases, substitutions, unions/intersections, utility/mapped/indexed forms, `typeof`, enums, and supported forms only until the closed answer is known. Object internals are not expanded merely to conclude `Object`.
   642	
   643	Current Svelte runtime compilation requests no native compile projection unless a future capability ADR proves an official semantic need.
   644	
   645	# 8. TypeInfo semantic kernel and public API
   646	
   647	## 8.1 One implementation
   648	
   649	`TypeInfoCore` owns:
   650	
   651	- authored-node traversal;
   652	- binder/name/reference semantics;
   653	- substitution;
   654	- relation/inference;
   655	- effective typing;
   656	- recursion/work budgets;
   657	- query-specific projection;
   658	- exactness/completeness propagation.
   659	
   660	`ModuleResolverCore` owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution. Environments supply observations; they do not implement semantics.
   661	
   662	Direct local, direct project, in-memory, managed, compile projection, component metadata, effective type, and framework surface operations share these kernels. Lifecycle adapters differ only in data access, concurrency, and retention.
   663	
   664	## 8.2 No final general `TypeExpr`, with ordered cutover
   665	
   666	The final architecture contains no general recursive owned `TypeExpr` or `PortableTypeExpr` as a generic semantic transit IR, final cache value, compile projection contract, or public result.
   667	
   668	The cutover is deliberately ordered:
   669	
   670	1. freeze every current producer and consumer, including `IndexedReady`/lazy body lowering, flow content, component-meta native/compat, graph export, NAPI/WASM DTOs, and tests;

     1	# A5 — Dependency-direction test strategy (locked)
     2	
     3	A5 locks the strategy; `B1` implements it ("Land the distinct identity/profile/mapping/
     4	result-contract types and **forbidden dependency-edge build tests**"). This file fixes *what kind
     5	of test*, *what it must reject*, and *what it replaces* — so `B1` cannot satisfy the requirement
     6	with a source scanner and cannot discover the real current violations mid-implementation.
     7	
     8	Binding authority: [`ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free`](../../decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md).
     9	
    10	---
    11	
    12	## 1. What enforces direction today
    13	
    14	| mechanism | location | kind |
    15	|---|---|---|
    16	| `dependency_closure_guard` | `crates/verter_macro_dto/tests/cases/dependency_closure_guard.rs` | **structural** — walks the real resolved graph from `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`, follows normal+build edges transitively, equality-pins the sanctioned `oxc_span` subtree |
    17	| `verter_audit_no_upward_deps` | `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs:11846` | TOML text scan of one manifest |
    18	| `audit_substrate_isolation` | `…architecture_guards.rs:11915` | source-text scan of `crates/verter_audit/src` for `verter_*` tokens |
    19	| `scheduler_does_not_depend_on_verter_session` / `scheduler_src_has_no_verter_session_path` | `crates/verter_scheduler/tests/cases/no_session_dep.rs` | manifest substring + source-text scan |
    20	| cargo itself | — | rejects dependency **cycles**; nothing else |
    21	
    22	Coverage today is **four crates out of thirty-nine** (`verter_macro_dto`, `verter_audit`,
    23	`verter_scheduler`, plus cargo's global cycle rule). Direction between the other thirty-five is
    24	enforced by review only.
    25	
    26	## 2. The locked strategy
    27	
    28	**One `cargo metadata`-driven forbidden-edge test over the whole workspace graph, modelled
    29	exactly on `verter_macro_dto`'s `dependency_closure_guard`. No new source-text scanner.**
    30	
    31	This is not a stylistic preference; it follows from `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only rule: *landed*
    32	enforcement is compiler/type-system/tool-based and never a name/text/grep scanner over the source
    33	tree. Three of the four mechanisms above are exactly the scanner form that rule grandfathers but
    34	forbids extending. The fourth is the model to generalise, and it is already the better test on the
    35	merits:
    36	
    37	- it reads what cargo actually links, so a forbidden edge added **behind any feature**, or
    38	  arriving **transitively**, fails — a manifest scan sees none of those;
    39	- it distinguishes production edges (normal + build) from dev-dependencies, so a guard's own
    40	  tooling dev-deps cannot self-trip it;
    41	- it pins its sanctioned exception by **equality** against a structurally computed set, so an
    42	  upstream release that grows the exception is a re-audit gate rather than a silent grant.
    43	
    44	Naming crates in a layer matrix is not the scanner failure mode the rule forbids. The rule's
    45	target is text matching over source; a resolve-graph walk over cargo's own output is the
    46	"real used tool" form it prescribes. The matrix is data for a graph query, not a grep pattern.
    47	
    48	### 2.1 Required properties of the `B1` test
    49	
    50	1. **Input** — `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`, the resolve cargo builds from.
    51	2. **Edges** — normal + build, transitive. Dev edges excluded and that exclusion stated.
    52	3. **Assertion form** — for each crate, its production closure must not reach any crate in a
    53	   strictly higher layer. Closure-based, not direct-edge-based: a direct-edge test passes while a
    54	   two-hop violation walks straight through it (§4 shows this is not hypothetical).
    55	4. **Exceptions** — equality-pinned, never subset-checked, each with a recorded rationale.
    56	5. **Discrimination** — the test must FAIL when a forbidden edge is added. `B1` proves it by
    57	   adding one to a scratch manifest and observing the failure, and the proof must show the
    58	   mutation was actually applied (`CLAUDE.md` → Verification Must Prove Execution: a plant that
    59	   fails to apply reports a pass).
    60	6. **Supersession, with one residue that must be decided rather than assumed.** Landing the
    61	   closure test deletes `verter_audit_no_upward_deps` and both tests in `no_session_dep.rs`:
    62	   their invariants are strictly implied by the walk (`verter_audit` closure ⊆
    63	   {`verter_audit`, `verter_span`}; `verter_scheduler` closure excludes `verter_session`), and
    64	   a source path reference to a non-dependency crate does not compile, so the source-scan half
    65	   adds nothing a closure walk misses. Keeping them would be a second authority for one rule,
    66	   and deleting them in the same accepted candidate is `CLAUDE.md`'s clean-cutover requirement.
    67	
    68	   `audit_substrate_isolation` is **not** fully implied, and `B1` must not delete it on the
    69	   assumption that it is. Its *dependency* half is implied. Its residue is a **naming** rule: it
    70	   rejects any `verter_*` token on a non-comment line in `crates/verter_audit/src`, including
    71	   ones that are not dependencies at all — that is exactly what it caught during A4, when the
    72	   scope macro's local binding `_verter_attribution_scope` tripped it. A closure walk cannot see
    73	   a local variable name. So `B1` decides explicitly: either the naming rule is worth keeping as
    74	   a separate, named, grandfathered guard, or it is dropped as coverage the program does not
    75	   need. Silently deleting it and calling the closure test a superset would lose real coverage.
    76	
    77	## 3. A5's proposed layer assignment
    78	
    79	ADR-015's chain, resolved to this workspace's crates. **`B1` ratifies this; A5 proposes it and
    80	supplies the evidence.**
    81	
    82	| layer | ADR-015 name | crates |
    83	|---|---|---|
    84	| 1 | identity / span / language / contracts | `verter_span`, `verter_language`, `verter_ecma`, `verter_analysis_inputs`, `verter_audit`, `verter_no_typeexpr`(+`_derive`), `verter_no_storedspan`(+`_derive`) |
    85	| 2 | shared syntax frontends + dependency-neutral DTOs | `verter_type_expr`, `verter_type_expr_oxc`, `verter_parser`, `verter_css_syntax`, `verter_macro_dto`, `verter_session_query` |
    86	| 3 | semantic kernel / module resolver / relation / flow | `verter_semantic`, `verter_diagnostics`, `verter_actions` |
    87	| 4 | compiler | `verter_compiler` |
    88	| 5 | managed engine / session | `verter_session`, `verter_workspace`, `verter_scheduler`, `verter_tsgo_api`, `verter_type_runtime`, `verter_protocol` |
    89	| 6 | adapters | `verter_lsp`, `verter_napi`, `verter_wasm`, `verter_ffi`, `verter_mcp`, `verter_mcp_server`, `verter_tsc`, `verter_relay_shim`, `verter-editor-client` |
    90	| 7 | harnesses (outside ADR-015; no crate may depend on these) | `verter_bench`, `verter_dx_baseline`, `verter_vue_conformance`, `verter_svelte_conformance`, `verter_session_oracle_macro` |
    91	
    92	Two placements need justification because they are the ones a reviewer will challenge:
    93	
    94	- **`verter_protocol` at layer 5, not layer 2.** ADR-015's layer 2 is *dependency-neutral* DTOs.
    95	  `verter_protocol` depends on `verter_semantic` (7 references, all
    96	  `analysis::component_meta::OrderedSfcStructureAnalysis` plus `refs`), so it is not neutral. It
    97	  is a transport projection above the kernel. `verter_macro_dto` is the crate that actually
    98	  satisfies layer 2's neutrality, and its closure guard proves it.
    99	- **`verter_audit` at layer 1.** Its production closure is exactly
   100	  `{verter_audit, verter_span}` — verified by closure walk. It is a leaf by construction.
   101	
   102	## 4. The two upward edges in the current tree
   103	
   104	Running the proposed matrix over the resolved graph yields **exactly two** production edges that
   105	point upward:
   106	
   107	```text
   108	L3 verter_semantic     ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
   109	L3 verter_diagnostics  ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
   110	```
   111	
   112	`verter_semantic` uses `verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead` (6 sites), `resolver`, `types`,
   113	`fact_registry`, and `FilesystemWorkspace`.
   114	
   115	**This is not repairable by re-layering.** The tempting fix — move `verter_workspace` down to
   116	layer 2 — fails, because `verter_workspace` itself depends on `verter_scheduler` and
   117	`verter_tsgo_api`. The two are declared differently, and `B1` must not conflate them
   118	(`crates/verter_workspace/Cargo.toml`):
   119	
   120	| dep | declaration | reach |
   121	|---|---|---|
   122	| `verter_scheduler` | `[dependencies]`, line 37 | unconditional — every target |
   123	| `verter_tsgo_api` | `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`, line 49 | native only; absent from a `wasm32` build |
   124	
   125	So the edge is real on every target, and its consequence is measurable — but the `verter_tsgo_api`
   126	half of that consequence is **native-only**:
   127	
   128	```text
   129	verter_semantic's production closure (--all-features, normal+build, transitive):
   130	  verter_audit  verter_css_syntax  verter_ecma  verter_language
   131	  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_parser
   132	  verter_scheduler  verter_span  verter_tsgo_api  verter_type_expr
   133	  verter_type_expr_oxc  verter_workspace
   134	```
   135	
   136	That closure is the `--all-features` **native** resolve, which is what `cargo metadata` reports by
   137	default and what the closure test will read.
   138	
   139	**The semantic kernel's production closure reaches the task scheduler unconditionally, and the
   140	external tsgo API on native targets.** ADR-015's stated consequence — "semantic kernel remains
   141	reusable across lifecycles" — does not hold today: linking the kernel links a task scheduler on
   142	every target, and additionally an out-of-process tool client on everything but `wasm32`. The
   143	platform split narrows the second half of the violation; it does not repair either half, because a
   144	`wasm32`-only firewall is not a firewall.
   145	
   146	Compare the crates that *do* satisfy their firewall:
   147	
   148	```text
   149	verter_audit      -> verter_audit  verter_span
   150	verter_macro_dto  -> verter_macro_dto  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_span
   151	```
   152	
   153	Reproduce all three with the closure walk over `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`,
   154	following `resolve.nodes[].deps` and skipping deps whose `dep_kinds` are all `dev`.
   155	
   156	### Disposition
   157	
   158	```text
   159	DEBT A5-DD1  Disposition: DEFER
   160	  Finding:          verter_semantic (and verter_diagnostics) depend on verter_workspace, so the
   161	                    semantic kernel's production closure reaches verter_scheduler (unconditional)
   162	                    and verter_tsgo_api (native only — declared under
   163	                    cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32")) in verter_workspace/Cargo.toml),
   164	                    contradicting ADR-015's reusability consequence
   165	  Durable owner:    C1 (converge ModuleResolverCore / non-flow TypeInfoCore — the block that
   166	                    decides what the kernel's input surface is), with B1 owning the test that
   167	                    makes the violation fail rather than be reviewed for
   168	  Resolution gate:  C1 accepted candidate. B1 MAY land its test with this pair as a recorded,
   169	                    equality-pinned exception; it MUST NOT land it as a subset-checked allowance,
   170	                    and the exception must name C1 as its removal gate.
   171	  Acceptance:       verter_semantic's closure contains neither verter_scheduler nor
   172	                    verter_tsgo_api on ANY target; the closure test fails if either returns.
   173	                    B1's equality-pinned exception must therefore record the target condition
   174	                    alongside the edge, so a wasm32-only resolve cannot read as satisfied.
   175	  Ruling reference: PENDING
   176	```
   177	
   178	The `B1`-may-land-with-exception clause matters: without it, `B1` either cannot land its own exit
   179	criterion or is tempted to weaken the test to green. The equality pin plus a named removal gate is
   180	what keeps a temporary exception from becoming permanent.
   181	
   182	## 5. What the strategy deliberately does not cover
   183	
   184	- **Intra-crate direction.** The closure walk sees crates. `verter_session` is 5 of the 6 layers
   185	  by volume, and the module-level direction inside it is not testable this way. ADR-015 is
   186	  explicit that "logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until
   187	  a real dependency firewall … exists" — so intra-crate direction is held by the type system
   188	  (privacy, sealed traits, the `NoTypeExpr` marker) and by review, not by this test. `K3` is the
   189	  block that turns the module boundaries that matter into crate boundaries.
   190	- **Trait-object back-edges.** A closure walk cannot see a callback that inverts control without
   191	  inverting the dependency. ADR-015 rejects "mutual compiler/semantic callbacks" for this reason;
   192	  detecting them is a review mandate, not a graph query.

     1	# C1 — Converge `ModuleResolverCore` and non-flow `TypeInfoCore`
     2	
     3	**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** Foundational
     4	(`program-dag.toml:162`). **Predecessors:** `A6`, `B1`, `B2` (`program-dag.toml:163`).
     5	
     6	C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
     7	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and the TypeScript-style resolver living in
     8	`verter_workspace::resolver` — into the two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a
     9	`ModuleResolverCore` that owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow
    10	`TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution,
    11	relation/inference, effective typing, recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and
    12	exactness/completeness propagation. Neither target type exists in code today; both names describe roles
    13	the current tree already plays under different names and in the wrong crate. C1 does not invent new
    14	resolution semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be
    15	identical to today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code, how many
    16	duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform I/O
    17	directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
    18	
    19	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
    20	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
    21	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
    22	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions. It owns
    23	convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, and the addition of a batched,
    24	resumable load-outcome so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume the same kernel a blocking lifecycle
    25	consumes today.
    26	
    27	## Intent Contract
    28	
    29	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
    30	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
    31	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
    32	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
    33	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation) and by omission (no lifecycle exists
    34	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), not by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits
    35	a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
    36	
    37	**Required observable outcomes.**
    38	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
    39	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
    40	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
    41	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
    42	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
    43	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
    44	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer.
    45	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_scheduler` nor
    46	  `verter_tsgo_api` on any target (closes debt row A5-DD1, `evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:158-176`).
    47	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (`resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:161`) has exactly as many
    48	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct lifecycles; a lifecycle that cannot
    49	  resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
    50	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
    51	
    52	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
    53	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
    54	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
    55	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832` — C1 preserves this unchanged).
    56	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
    57	  observation views").
    58	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
    59	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext` implementor served it, for
    60	  identical inputs.
    61	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
    62	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
    63	
    64	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
    65	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
    66	point). `ResolverContext` implementors are lifecycle *adapters* over that one authority, never alternate
    67	authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed
    68	non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s `CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split,
    69	`.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) — C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken
    70	it while adding the `NeedInputs` outcome alongside it.

   127	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract
   128	
   129	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
   130	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
   131	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   132	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
   133	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
   134	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet"
   135	crates/` — zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
   136	
   137	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
   138	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
   139	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
   140	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
   141	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
   142	C1's obligation ends at: one resolver-tier operation, one immutable snapshot, one typed outcome. C2's
   143	obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay
   144	tokens.
   145	
   146	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
   147	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
   148	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
   149	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome so a *new* I/O-free lifecycle can reuse the same resolution
   150	logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every existing call site to stop blocking.
   151

   187	## Structural confinement
   188	
   189	Every invariant above is enforced structurally, matching the pattern the codebase already uses in this
   190	exact area — C1 extends that pattern, it does not invent scanner-based enforcement:
   191	
   192	- **Sealed-trait lifecycle closure.** `ResolverContext: sealed::Sealed` (`resolver_context.rs:82-98,161`)
   193	  already makes "some fourth, unregistered lifecycle adapter" a compile error. C1 preserves the seal and,
   194	  if the bare-host rail is deleted (see above), tightens `RequestBoundResolverContext`
   195	  (`resolver_context.rs:780-815`, `static_assertions::assert_obj_safe!`) from "narrower than
   196	  `ResolverContext`" to "identical to it" — a resolver-tier function taking `&dyn ResolverContext` becomes
   197	  provably request-bound by construction, not by convention.
   198	- **`StoreView`/`HostStoreView` immutability is already structural**, not a convention: `HostStoreView`
   199	  (`resolver_store.rs:1462-1525`) has no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<..>>` field, only `Arc`-shared by-value
   200	  snapshot data; a future violation (a live host reference smuggled into the struct) is a visible field
   201	  addition a reviewer catches at the type definition, not a runtime behavior to detect.
   202	- **The Authority-uniqueness contract** (`.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832`: no second
   203	  `SemanticQueryApi` impl, no second `execute_relate`, no second `shallow_lower_type_expr`, no second
   204	  `RelationMemo` owner, no second semantic-node-map owner) is enforced today partly by a `syn`-AST content
   205	  scanner (`crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs:3384` `mod resolver_context_seal`,
   206	  reached from `no_concrete_verter_host_in_seal_scope` at `:3703-3712`) and partly by grandfathered
   207	  string-content assertions (e.g. `resolver_store_view_returns_store_view_read` at `:16454-16469`). Per
   208	  `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only landed-scanner rule, these are **grandfathered, not a template**: C1 must not
   209	  add a new name-keyed source scanner for any *new* invariant it introduces (the deleted bare-host rail,
   210	  the collapsed duplication, the new `AttemptOutcome`). New confinement is type-level: privacy, the
   211	  existing seal, a marker type for "I/O-free context" analogous to `RequestBoundResolverContext`, or a
   212	  `NoTypeExpr`-style content-free marker if `AttemptOutcome<T>` needs one. C1 may *extend* the existing
   213	  grandfathered scanners' checked assertions if a change under review genuinely regresses what they
   214	  already check; it may not add a new standalone scanner test.
   215	- **`NeedInputs` non-blocking guarantee.** The cleanest structural proof available is a marker type on the
   216	  I/O-free context (e.g. an `IoFreeResolverContext` sealed subtrait, mirroring
   217	  `RequestBoundResolverContext`'s shape) that is never implemented for any type holding a `&VerterHost`
   218	  capable of reaching the scheduler — so a resolver-tier function generic over that marker cannot call
   219	  `ensure_loaded` even if someone tries, because the trait bound does not expose it. This is a design
   220	  recommendation, not a locked mechanism; see Open Questions.
   221	
   222	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
   223	
   224	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
   225	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
   226	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
   227	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
   228	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
   229	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges remains the single authority `D1`
   230	integrates against behind its private non-production test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later
   231	extends without needing a second relation/name authority (`program.md:253`: "No flow-private relation/name
   232	authority may exist after `D2`"). If convergence work touches `project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`,
   233	`relation_txn.rs`, or the `RelationMemo` at all, it is confined to lifecycle/context plumbing around the
   234	call, never the relation algorithm itself.
   235	
   236	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
   237	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
   238	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
   239	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
   240	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is: a `ResolverContext`-shaped kernel
   241	(or its post-extraction equivalent) that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be driven
   242	from an I/O-free environment and returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking, and (c) can be constructed
   243	without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery, so C2's compiler-facing
   244	facade does not have to depend on the whole `verter_session` crate to embed it.
   245	
   246	## Required exit
   247	
   248	Per `program.md:196`: **lifecycle differs; module/name/type/relation meaning does not.** Concretely: the
   249	three (or more, once the I/O-free context exists) `ResolverContext` implementors give bit-identical
   250	resolved answers for identical inputs; the duplicated boilerplate between `HostResolverContext` and
   251	`SessionResolverContext` is gone; `verter_semantic`'s production closure excludes `verter_scheduler` and
   252	`verter_tsgo_api` on every target with no exception recorded; `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` exists
   253	and is exercised by at least one real resolver-tier load point without touching the scheduler; the
   254	Authority-uniqueness contract's five rows still hold; no `TypeExpr`-general transit, flow semantics, or
   255	C2-owned staged-transaction machinery was introduced.

   277	## Open questions requiring maintainer/architecture ruling
   278	
   279	These are gaps this research could not close from the code and evidence tree alone. Do not dispatch
   280	implementation against them without a ruling — each is a real design fork, not a detail:
   281	
   282	1. **Crate placement.** `resolver_core`/`resolver_store` are today private modules inside `verter_session`
   283	   with no crate boundary between them (confirmed: `lib.rs:341-344`, plain `use crate::resolver_store::…`
   284	   intra-crate references throughout). `architecture.md` §18.1 places "semantic kernel/module
   285	   resolver/relation/flow" *below* "compiler" and far below "managed engine/session" in the inward
   286	   dependency chain, which today's placement inverts. Whether C1 must physically extract the converged
   287	   kernel into a new crate (and if so, its name, its exact member boundary, and whether extraction happens
   288	   inside C1 or is staged into a follow-up block C1 merely proves is possible) is the single largest open
   289	   design question in this charter. I did not find an existing target crate name or extraction plan in
   290	   `architecture.md`, the ADRs, or `program-dag.toml` — this needs an explicit pre-implementation
   291	   architecture challenge (governance.md's Foundational-class requirement), not a decision made inside
   292	   the charter.
   293	2. **A5-DD1's harder half.** `verter_semantic/src/analysis/routes.rs`'s `&dyn verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead`
   294	   parameter (6 call sites) is a genuine functional dependency, not a re-export. Closing the
   295	   `verter_semantic → verter_workspace` edge requires either relocating `WorkspaceRead` to a lower neutral
   296	   layer or moving route-extraction logic upward to where `WorkspaceRead` already lives — I could not
   297	   determine from the code which is correct without risking a guess that contradicts `F1`'s
   298	   not-yet-written committed-input-authority design. Flagged, not resolved, in Legacy Deletions above.
   299	3. **Whether `NeedInputs` needs a structural (marker-type) non-blocking guarantee or an accepted
   300	   review-enforced one.** I recommend a sealed `IoFreeResolverContext`-shaped marker (mirroring
   301	   `RequestBoundResolverContext`) so a resolver-tier function generic over it cannot reach
   302	   `ensure_loaded`/the scheduler even by accident, but this is materially more invasive than a
   303	   review-enforced convention and its cost/benefit was not evaluated against a real implementation attempt.
   304	   This should be settled at the same pre-implementation architecture challenge as (1), since the answer
   305	   likely depends on it (a marker type is far cheaper to add correctly if the extraction in (1) happens
   306	   first, because the I/O-free context would then live outside `verter_session` entirely and could not
   307	   physically hold a `&VerterHost`).
   308	4. **Scope of "AttemptOutcome" coverage.** `program.md:196` says "return batched `NeedInputs`" without
   309	   qualifying which resolver-tier operations. This charter scopes it to the load points already reached
   310	   through `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` (the only synchronous-blocking-on-I/O sites this
   311	   research found). Whether C2 needs *every* resolver-core query to support the outcome on day one, or
   312	   whether a narrower first cut (module/import resolution only, deferring full type-query coverage) is
   313	   acceptable, is a scope call for whoever authors C1's pre-implementation brief — I have not sized the

     1	# Snapshot-Consistent Batched Input Loading Contract
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative outer-orchestration contract.
     4	
     5	# 1. Kernel rule
     6	
     7	The compiler, resolver, TypeInfo, flow, and reusable query kernels consume one immutable observation view per attempt and perform no hidden filesystem/network/process/package-manager I/O.
     8	
     9	# 2. Outcome
    10	
    11	```rust
    12	enum AttemptOutcome<T> {
    13	    Complete(T),
    14	    NeedInputs(LoadSet),
    15	    Terminal(AttemptFailure),
    16	}
    17	```
    18	
    19	`LoadSet` is normalized, sorted, deduplicated, and includes the resolution basis needed to load/commit safely. The kernel discovers all independently reachable missing observations it can identify without fabricating semantic answers.
    20	
    21	# 3. Orchestration state
    22	
    23	```text
    24	attempt number
    25	current snapshot identity
    26	accumulated requested InputKeys
    27	accumulated stable positive/negative observations
    28	unique input count
    29	loaded byte count
    30	dependency depth/frontier
    31	basis-change/churn count
    32	```
    33	
    34	# 4. Algorithm
    35	
    36	1. Run the whole operation against snapshot `S`.
    37	2. On `Complete`, validate observed facts against `S` and return/admit according to the query contract.
    38	3. On `Terminal`, return typed failure and never admit complete state.
    39	4. On `NeedInputs(L)`, normalize `L` and calculate `delta = L.keys - accumulated_requested`.
    40	5. If `delta` is empty and neither the resolution basis nor any previously observed fact changed, return `InputResolutionNoProgress` with the unresolved set.
    41	6. Check configured limits before I/O: attempts, unique keys, bytes, dependency depth, and basis-change/churn count.
    42	7. Load `delta` through embedding-owned same-key I/O flights. Each result is `Present`, stable `Missing`, or transient `LoadFailure`, with typed metadata and basis. Public/external loader digests are hints: the committing authority verifies key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints from captured data before publication.
    43	8. Conditionally publish all validated commit-eligible observations as one coherent input batch only if the project/configuration basis remains compatible.
    44	9. If conditional commit loses a race or the basis changed, capture the new coherent snapshot, increment churn budget, and restart. Do not splice data into the old attempt.
    45	10. If committed, capture the new snapshot and restart from step 1.
    46	
    47	# 5. Direct project mode
    48	
    49	A direct/project `CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns `NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry. The same no-progress/resource rules apply to convenience orchestration APIs.
    50	
    51	# 6. Observation trust boundary
    52	
    53	- public environments/loaders cannot mint authoritative `ContentId`, `InputBasisId`, semantic read facts, or completeness evidence;
    54	- source bytes, declared language/source type, canonical source identity, package/config metadata, lengths, and supplied digests are consistency-checked at capture/commit;
    55	- the authoritative owner hashes/normalizes once per committed revision and reuses the typed IDs thereafter;
    56	- a sealed first-party `EngineSnapshot` may carry prevalidated IDs because the same authority minted them;
    57	- mismatched key/bytes/profile/basis is a typed integrity failure and is never cached as stable missing or complete.
    58	
    59	# 7. Negative facts
    60	
    61	A stable missing module/package/file may be observed and cached only with the complete resolution basis: parent/package boundaries, conditions, path/case/symlink/workspace policy, and relevant configuration. Transient permission/network/process/provider failure is not a stable negative semantic fact.
    62	
    63	# 8. Resource failures
    64	
    65	Distinct failures include:
    66	
    67	```text
    68	InputResolutionNoProgress
    69	InputResolutionAttemptLimit
    70	InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit
    71	InputResolutionByteLimit
    72	InputResolutionDepthLimit
    73	InputResolutionChurnLimit
    74	InputLoadUnavailable
    75	InputCommitConflictExceeded
    76	```
    77	
    78	They carry unresolved keys and consumed budget without exposing sensitive ambient paths beyond the product's diagnostic policy.
    79	
    80	# 9. Tests
    81	
    82	- multiple missing siblings loaded in one batch;
    83	- transitive dependency waves;
    84	- stable missing negative fact;
    85	- dependency appears between attempts;
    86	- project/config changes during load;
    87	- repeated same `LoadSet` no progress;
    88	- loader partial/transient failure;
    89	- unique key/byte/depth/retry/churn limits;
    90	- external observation digest/key mismatch rejected before commit;
    91	- no semantic kernel I/O instrumentation;
    92	- final result equals an equivalent fully preloaded clean run.
     1	# Staged Compile Transaction and Anti-Replay Contract
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative direct/prepared/project-aware compiler protocol.
     4	
     5	# 1. Stages
     6	
     7	```text
     8	prepare(source, parse options)
     9	  -> PreparedCarrier
    10	plan(prepared, CompileRequest)
    11	  -> CompilePlan
    12	project(plan.projection_batch, CompileTypeInfo)
    13	  -> CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure
    14	emit(prepared, plan, complete facts)
    15	  -> CompileResult
    16	```
    17	
    18	Planning discovers the complete product prerequisite closure and closed semantic projection batch before projection. Emission does not discover new project-semantic demands. A new demand requires a new plan.
    19	
    20	# 2. Binding tokens
    21	
    22	`CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay. The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens:
    23	
    24	```text
    25	ProjectionPlanToken   root + semantic profile + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains
    26	ProductSubplanToken   root + framework/product + output profile + required product mapping contract
    27	TerminalSubplanToken  exact typed result/product + requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile
    28	```
    29	
    30	The whole `CompilePlanToken` binds at least:
    31	
    32	- prepared root/source/unit identities;
    33	- parse key/domain and relevant generation;
    34	- normalized canonical typed product-request collection;
    35	- shared semantic profile when observed;
    36	- each product's output and requested terminal presentation/mapping/provenance/serialization profiles;
    37	- framework/compiler compatibility identity;
    38	- projection schema/domain;
    39	- plan algorithm compatibility domain;
    40	- deterministic demand ordering and digest.
    41	
    42	The plan contains independently keyed subplans/artifact identities. A presentation-, map-encoding-, provenance-, or serialization-only change may create a new terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic projection or code-generation subplan. `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay; it does not force every subartifact to use that whole token as its cache key.
    43	
    44	`CompileFactsBatch` binds:
    45	
    46	- exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest referenced by the containing plan;
    47	- semantic profile and kernel compatibility domain;
    48	- input basis and observed dependency fingerprints;
    49	- one typed result for every demand;
    50	- exactness/completeness/degradation;
    51	- integrity and size limits when decoded or transferred.
    52	
    53	Emission first validates the whole `CompilePlanToken`, then validates that the facts satisfy the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` referenced by that plan. It rejects missing, extra, duplicated, reordered without canonical identity, stale, wrong-profile, wrong-projection-plan, wrong-root, wrong-domain, or insufficient facts before output construction.
    54	
    55	# 3. Zero-demand behavior
    56	
    57	When the plan has no semantic projection demands:
    58	
    59	- no `CompileTypeInfo` session is constructed;
    60	- no module resolver or TypeInfo index/graph/flow work runs;
    61	- projection stage is represented as an empty complete batch bound to the plan;
    62	- Svelte current runtime compilation must prove zero Vue/native projection demand unless its capability contract changes.
    63	
    64	# 4. `NeedInputs`
    65	
    66	`NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a resumable orchestration outcome. It does not mutate the current plan or prepared value with unversioned ambient data. The outer orchestrator loads and publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view according to `input-loading.md`, then reruns projection with the same plan only when the plan’s source/request/profile basis remains valid. Otherwise it replans.
    67	
    68	# 5. Direct and managed modes
    69	
    70	- local direct mode may project from the retained root only;
    71	- direct project mode consumes an immutable caller-provided observation view and returns `NeedInputs` to the caller;
    72	- managed mode consumes one `EngineSnapshot`/`InputBasisId` per attempt and uses the outer commit/retry loop;
    73	- all modes execute one semantic kernel and the same closed framework projector;
    74	- lifecycle, retention, and orchestration differ; semantics do not.
    75	
    76	# 6. Error taxonomy
    77	
    78	Distinct failures include parse/preparation failure, unsupported product combination, unavailable semantic capability, `NeedInputs`, no progress, projection gap, unresolved dependency, stale plan/facts, profile/domain mismatch, size/integrity failure, cancellation, budget exhaustion, and internal failure.
    79	
    80	# 7. Required tests
    81	
    82	- plan once and emit multiple requested products without rediscovery;
    83	- simultaneous product combinations equal separately requested products where contracts declare composability;
    84	- different per-product output profiles coexist without a global-profile collision;
    85	- presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans;
    86	- irrelevant product/profile fields are rejected or normalized away before identity construction;
    87	- zero-demand zero-initialization;
    88	- local and imported projection batches;
    89	- batched shared-root deduplication;
    90	- stale/wrong-whole-plan/wrong-projection-plan/wrong-profile/extra/missing facts rejected;
    91	- facts from a terminal-only sibling plan are accepted only when their `ProjectionPlanToken` is exactly equal;
    92	- `NeedInputs` waves and no-progress behavior;
    93	- basis change forces retry/replan as appropriate;
    94	- direct/prepared/managed output equality for equal product/profile/input contracts;
    95	- cancelled/superseded attempts do not terminally materialize output.

     1	# ADR-003 — Compile Semantics Use a Concrete Sealed Facade
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted
     4	
     5	## Context
     6	
     7	The compiler needs optional project-aware semantic projections. An open trait would permit alternate module/type/runtime-classification semantics and create a second engine.
     8	
     9	## Decision
    10	
    11	The compiler accepts only a concrete Verter-owned `CompileTypeInfo<'_>` facade. Lifecycle variants are private/sealed first-party constructions. External integrations may supply captured observations through a data-only environment; they cannot implement semantic behavior.
    12	
    13	All construction modes execute one profile-parameterized semantic kernel and one module resolver. The facade has no blanket `Send + Sync`; ownership/concurrency is a lifecycle policy.
    14	
    15	## Consequences
    16	
    17	Direct local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes remain possible without opening semantics or coupling the compiler to `Engine`.
    18	
    19	## Rejected alternatives
    20	
    21	- public semantic trait object;
    22	- compiler receives host/Engine/provider state;
    23	- framework/compiler-local resolver fallback.
     1	# ADR-011 — Project-Aware Compile Uses a Resumable I/O-Free Transaction
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** direct compiler/project TypeInfo integration  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a future compiler mode explicitly embeds I/O and accepts a separate architecture boundary.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	A compile API that may need project inputs cannot safely hide I/O or retain OXC borrows across asynchronous loading. Projection facts must be proven to belong to the exact plan that consumes them.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	Project-aware compile follows:
    14	
    15	```text
    16	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
    17	```
    18	
    19	- prepared syntax remains owned/borrowed by one retained owner;
    20	- the projection batch is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
    21	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root; the plan contains narrower deterministic projection/product/terminal subplan tokens;
    22	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, projection schema, and demand digest, so terminal-only sibling plans may reuse facts only when that projection token is exactly equal;
    23	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome;
    24	- external loading occurs outside compiler/semantic compute;
    25	- no syntax borrow or unvalidated locator crosses the loading boundary;
    26	- each attempt reports the maximal sound missing observation set discovered;
    27	- retries use a monotonic progress ledger, bounded waves/resources, and deterministic no-progress failure;
    28	- stale or replayed facts are rejected before emission.
    29	
    30	## Consequences
    31	
    32	The same semantic kernel supports local, captured-project, in-memory, and managed-snapshot modes without hidden filesystem authority.
    33	
    34	## Rejected alternatives
    35	
    36	- **Synchronous hidden filesystem callbacks:** break hermeticity and coherent snapshots.
    37	- **Reparse/replan implicitly after every missing input:** can amplify work and consume mismatched facts.
     1	# ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** crate/module ownership  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a new stable boundary cannot be represented without a cycle and an alternative decomposition has been disproven.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	Where `CompileTypeInfo`, framework projection DTOs, and request contracts live can accidentally create compiler↔semantic or compiler↔session cycles, forcing traits, erasure, and shared ownership.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	Binding direction is:
    14	
    15	```text
    16	identity/span/language/contracts
    17	-> shared syntax frontends and dependency-neutral DTOs
    18	-> semantic kernel/module resolver/relation/flow
    19	-> compiler
    20	-> managed engine/session
    21	-> LSP/provider/MCP/NAPI/WASM/CLI adapters
    22	```
    23	
    24	Rules:
    25	
    26	- syntax/contracts do not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    27	- semantic kernel does not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    28	- compiler may depend on syntax, sealed semantic facade, and neutral closed DTOs;
    29	- managed engine depends on compiler/semantic, never the reverse;
    30	- provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel;
    31	- adapters depend inward only;
    32	- durable build tests reject crate dependency cycles and forbidden edges.
    33	
    34	Logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until a real dependency firewall or multi-consumer stable contract exists.
    35	
    36	## Consequences
    37	
    38	- direct compiler cannot become a session mode;
    39	- semantic kernel remains reusable across lifecycles;
    40	- fewer traits, erased bags, and `Arc` workarounds are required.
    41	
    42	## Rejected alternatives
    43	
    44	- **Mutual compiler/semantic callbacks:** creates cycles and alternate behavior.
    45	- **Everything in session/host crate:** preserves catch-all ownership.
     1	# ADR-001 — One Semantic Authority, Justified Derived Projections
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** TypeInfo/effective-flow architecture
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	`FunctionFlowGraph` must be the one structural flow authority, but efficient solving may need dominators, loop forests, SCCs, def-use overlays, capture summaries, reverse adjacency, or compact execution schedules. Forbidding every graph-derived structure would either bloat the canonical graph or repeat topology work. Allowing independent query-specific CFGs recreates the current dual-authority defect.
     9	
    10	## Decision
    11	
    12	`FunctionFlowGraph` is the canonical structural authority. A derived structure is allowed only when it:
    13	
    14	- is keyed by one exact graph/body identity and any interpretation-affecting semantic profile;
    15	- is deterministic and fully reproducible from the graph and accepted kernel rules;
    16	- cannot add facts, define transfer/join semantics, mark coverage complete, or publish a semantic result;
    17	- is request-local by default and independently weighted/evicted if retention is proven valuable;
    18	- can be replaced without changing observable semantics.
    19	
    20	## Consequences
    21	
    22	The solver may use efficient layouts without creating a second semantic or control authority. Review checks authority and construction rights, not superficial data-structure count.
    23	
    24	## Rejected alternatives
    25	
    26	- exactly one physical graph-like object;
    27	- independent syntax-shaped/query-specific CFGs;
    28	- projections that own relation, completion, capture, or coverage decisions.

   475	### Verification Must Prove Execution (MANDATORY)
   476	
   477	A required gate passes only on fresh, input-bound evidence that: every applicable required job was eligible and ran; the intended tree-derived surface was owned and independently discovered; selectors matched non-zero work; required source, build, and fixture prerequisites matched the tested tree; executed work was non-zero; unexpected prerequisite skips were zero; child deadlines were strictly below their parent killer; and a terminal summary completed. **Exit status 0 alone, a self-declared test universe, or a missing required-job result is FAIL.** Every tracked test or guard has exactly one declared primary gate; a hand-maintained filename list may not define the primary universe unless generated from independent discovery and parity-checked.
   478	
   479	Attestation alone is insufficient — a receipt faithfully attests whatever incomplete universe the runner defines for itself. The durable design needs all three: fresh execution attestation; independently tree-derived inventory/discovery parity; and per-surface negative-control mutation through the exact canonical entry point. A single global canary cannot detect an omitted unrelated spec.

Prove the mutation is present, unique, and new in the source before trusting the run; a green planted run means the plant failed until proven otherwise. A discrimination check that cannot distinguish "the plant did not apply" from "the code is correct" is not a discrimination check.

528:**Intent before mechanism.** Before mechanism design for a block that changes observable behavior, authority, or fallback, record a ratified intent contract: the actor/problem and why the capability should exist; required and forbidden observable outcomes; authority/fallback order; a planned test or gate for each stable acceptance ID; and material cold, warm, allocation, fan-out, and latency bounds. An internal substrate block may reference its parent contract but must state the invariant and performance contribution it owns. Ratification comes from the approved plan or product authority; no implementation brief is dispatched without it. Enforcement is judgment — exercised at decomposition and again immediately before implementation dispatch.
532:Execute approved plans fully in one pass, end-to-end, without intermediate checkpoints or mid-plan confirmation on already-approved steps. Do not pause, defer scope, leave planned work unfinished, or rewrite the plan into a smaller/safer variant because the correct path is breaking, broad, or labor-intensive. Approved plans land as written unless the user explicitly re-scopes them.
534:**One-pass execution applies only while the approved design remains valid.** The second-REOPEN circuit breaker lapses approval for the affected design: pause implementation, obtain and record the required architecture/product ruling, and resume only once the design is ratified again. This is not a checkpoint — one-pass governs *executing an approved design*, and the breaker fires when *approval itself has lapsed*, which is a different event and precisely why execution must stop rather than grind on. STOP, failed verification, rule conflict, and verified plan-invalidating discoveries pause at their prescribed evidence gate without creating a discretionary user checkpoint. Breadth, breakage, effort, or migration size never lapses approval; approved scope changes only through the recorded ruling or explicit user re-scope. See `/mom-cto-orchestration` → Decision Admission.

   255	    /// boundary crate is still counted as reached; its own deps are not.
   256	    /// Separates a crate's own upward edges from reach inherited through
   257	    /// an already-excepted violator.
   258	    fn production_closure_names_with_boundary(
   259	        &self,
   260	        root_name: &str,
   261	        boundary: &BTreeSet<&str>,
   262	    ) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   263	        let root = self.id_of(root_name).to_string();
   264	        let mut seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
   265	        let mut queue: VecDeque<String> = VecDeque::new();
   266	        seen.insert(root.clone());
   267	        queue.push_back(root);
   268	        let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
   269	        while let Some(id) = queue.pop_front() {
   270	            // Reached, but do not walk its deps.
   271	            if boundary.contains(self.name_of(&id)) && id != self.id_of(root_name) {
   272	                continue;
   273	            }
   274	            let deps = self
   275	                .production_deps
   276	                .get(&id)
   277	                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("resolve graph must carry a node for `{id}`"));
   278	            for (dep, _target) in deps {
   279	                if seen.insert(dep.clone()) {
   280	                    names.insert(self.name_of(dep).to_string());
   281	                    queue.push_back(dep.clone());
   282	                }
   283	            }
   284	        }
   285	        names
   286	    }
